articles.title: Maresca claims City spending necessary to match Arsenal
articles.summary: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says the club must spend to match Arsenal.
articles.content:
Maresca claims City spending necessary to match Arsenal

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says the club must spend to match Arsenal.

Last Update:

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has defended the club’s £450 million summer spending spree, insisting the overhaul was necessary if they are to challenge Arsenal for the Premier League title.

City completed a major rebuild during the transfer window, with deadline-day arrivals Enzo Fernandez and Iliman Ndiaye making their debuts in Sunday’s 1-0 win over Coventry.

The pair were the final additions to a squad that has undergone significant changes, with City spending more than £450 million during the summer.

Maresca believes the depth available to Arsenal shows why City needed to strengthen their own squad if they are serious about competing at the top of the table.

“If you see since the Community Shield, Arsenal play two more games [against Coventry and Aston Villa] and they have five changes in every game,” Maresca said.

“Two World Cup winners, [Mikel] Merino and [Martin] Zubimendi, two England players, [Eberechi] Eze and [Noni] Madueke, and the other one I don’t remember, I think it was [Piero] Hincapie.

“In the end, if you want to be there you need options. Arsenal have options. We have options. More teams have options so it’s not just us. I’m very happy with the options we have, that is something important for us if you want to compete.”

Maresca praises Anderson’s attitude

Maresca was particularly impressed by Anderson’s approach since joining the club, highlighting his willingness to learn as well as his performances on the pitch.

“Really impressed, but not just today,” Maresca said.

“He was very good against Palace. He was also very good against Bournemouth having only been one week with us when we changed him for cramp.

“But the best thing with Elliot is the day by day. He is asking how he can learn, we sit with him in one-on-one video [analysis] and he wants to be better and that is the best thing for any player.”

City have won all three of their Premier League matches under Maresca so far and currently sit among the early challengers at the top of the table.

articles.title: Premier League round-up: Draws for Brighton and Brentford as Palace win thriller
articles.summary: Catch up with the action from Saturday afternoon's Premier League games.
articles.content:
Premier League round-up: Draws for Brighton and Brentford as Palace win thriller

Catch up with the action from Saturday afternoon's Premier League games.

Last Update:

Table of Contents

Brentford 1-1 Sunderland

A Vitaly Janelt goal and an Enzo Le Fee penalty shared the spoils at the Gtech Community Stadium in a match that both sides will feel they could have won.

Janelt gave Brentford the lead in the 57th minute, arriving from deep to steer a composed finish past Anthony Patterson, and Keith Andrews’ side looked on course for their second home win of the season.

Sunderland, however, refused to fold. With eight minutes remaining, Le Fee stepped up to convert from 12 yards, drawing the visitors level.

Both teams finish the afternoon on four points after three games. Kevin Schade has led the line with real threat for Brentford and continues to generate the most chances of any Bee this season, while Igor Thiago pressed and harassed throughout.

Brighton 1-1 Leeds

Leeds extended their unbeaten start to the Premier League season with a hard-earned point at the Amex, though Joel Bogle will consider himself lucky to have still been on the pitch when he opened the scoring.

The right-back was shown a yellow card in the sixth minute for a serious foul play challenge on Maxim De Cuyper that could quite easily have resulted in red, and the controversy lingered over the opening exchanges.

But Bogle made amends in the 15th minute, converting coolly from Ao Tanaka’s delivery to give Leeds an unexpected lead.

Brighton, who dominated possession as they have done in both previous league fixtures this season, pushed with increasing urgency in the second half and eventually levelled to take a share of the spoils.

Fabian Hurzeler’s side have now scored in both home games and shown genuine attacking threat, but conceding first has been a recurring problem that will need addressing.

Fulham 2-3 Crystal Palace

Crystal Palace claimed their first Premier League win of the season in dramatic fashion at Craven Cottage, coming from behind to beat Fulham 3-2.

Fulham had fought their way in front at 2-1 through Cesar Palacios, a goal that seemed to give Alvaro Arbeloa’s side the platform they desperately needed after two opening defeats.

But Palace, also without a point going into the afternoon, refused to accept the situation and produced a rousing finale.

Ben Chilwell was the match-winner, turning the tie on its head with the goal that made it 3-2 and prompted scenes of celebration from the travelling contingent at Craven Cottage.

articles.title: Barnes hits beauty but Bournemouth dominate at Newcastle
articles.summary: Three goals in a thrilling first half
articles.content:
Barnes hits beauty but Bournemouth dominate at Newcastle

Three goals in a thrilling first half

Last Update:

Bournemouth put in a superb first-half showing to lead Newcastle 2-1 at the break of the early Premier League game.

The Cherries were relentless in their pressing and attacking and fired into a 2-0 lead through Marcus Tavernier and a Malick Thiaw own goal.

Newcastle looked shocked but Harvey Barnes gave them some hope before half time with a fantastic curler.

The visitors went ahead when Rayan made a run and cross down the left. When Alex Scott’s shot on the egde of the box was blocked, the ball span kindly into the path of Tavernier to bury from close rnage.

Justin Kluivert had a shot well charged down as Scott ran the show.

Another rapid attack came from Scott winning the ball back. Kluivert hit the post with a stunning long range strike and when Scott retrieved the ball to fire it across goal it struck Thiaw and looped in.

The home crowd were incensed but Barnes then instantly reduced the deficit with a cracking curling shot after cutting in from the left.

articles.title: Liverpool sporting director Hughes leaves Anfield with Al Hilal move on the cards
articles.summary: Reds looking for new sporting director after transfer window closes
articles.content:
Liverpool sporting director Hughes leaves Anfield with Al Hilal move on the cards

Reds looking for new sporting director after transfer window closes

Last Update:

Liverpool sporting director Richard Hughes has stepped down from his position at Anfield, bringing an end to a two-year stint that saw the Reds capture their 20th title.

Hughes, 47, is reportedly poised to take up a lucrative sporting director role with Saudi Pro League champions Al-Hilal. The move will see Hughes reunite with former AFC Bournemouth technical director Simon Francis in Riyadh.

Al-Hilal have orchestrated an aggressive raid on the Premier League in recent windows, splashing out massive fees to land Gabriel Martinelli from Arsenal, Ollie Watkins from Aston Villa, and Crysencio Summerville from West Ham United.

Appointed from Bournemouth in June 2024, Hughes arrived during a period of massive transition at Anfield. Working alongside former head coach Arne Slot, Hughes helped deliver immediate domestic success with the 2024-25 Premier League crown.

Speaking on behalf of the club’s ownership, FSG president Mike Gordon praised Hughes’ leadership throughout a crucial chapter in modern club history:

“Richard joined us at the start of a period of change, embracing that responsibility by leading our football operations department and overseeing recruitment while also providing valuable support to our coaching staff,” he said.

“The results we achieved in these areas during this period are testament to this contribution. Nevertheless, we respect Richard’s life choices and wish him and his family well in their next venture.”

In an official farewell statement, Hughes expressed deep gratitude to the Anfield hierarchy, staff, and fanbase:

“First and foremost, I would like to reiterate what I said upon my arrival – it has been a source of great pride to have been given the opportunity to serve this incredible and unique institution. That is something I will always be grateful for.

“My appreciation extends to ownership for their support and leadership, to club staff at all levels who give so much to make Liverpool FC what it is, to the players who make such an enormous contribution and to the fans who support the team in great numbers whenever and wherever games take place.

“I’ll always follow and support the club with great affection, and I wish everyone involved nothing but success for this season and beyond.”

articles.title: Mourinho: ‘Sometimes you lose and you can’t explain it’
articles.summary: Real were beaten for the first time this season by Betis
articles.content:
Mourinho: ‘Sometimes you lose and you can’t explain it’

Real were beaten for the first time this season by Betis

Last Update:

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho said he had no complaints with his side’s performance as they were beaten 1-0 by Real Betis on Friday night.

Republic of Ireland striker Troy Parrott scored his first La Liga goal and Alvaro Valles saved a late Kylian Mbappe penalty to deny Real.

Mourinho, whose side are now level on nine points with both Betis and Barcelona, was happy with his team despite tasting defeat for the first time this season.

He said: “I think the team played a great game. Sometimes you lose and you don’t know how to explain it.

“We were very dominant with a lot of attacking play. If it had ended in a draw, we would have been frustrated.”

Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Jr all hit the woodwork on a frustrating night for Real which also led to Mourinho being shown a yellow card.

He said: “I don’t know why I saw a yellow card. I accept it. I stood up because a Betis player looked like he’d died in front of the bench.

“I saw a lot of people frustrated with the plays, but I didn’t see it myself and I can’t comment. The referee let the game flow, and that’s something I like.

“I don’t know why we lost because collectively we played very well. I have nothing to reproach any player for regarding their attitude. We deserved to win, but deserving doesn’t get you points.”

articles.title: Iraola hails Isak after first Liverpool win at Ipswich: ‘He’s a massive player for us’
articles.summary: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has heaped praise on Alexander Isak
articles.content:
Iraola hails Isak after first Liverpool win at Ipswich: ‘He’s a massive player for us’

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has heaped praise on Alexander Isak

Last Update:

Andoni Iraola praised the impact of Alexander Isak and the discipline of his Liverpool side after a dominant 2-0 win at Ipswich Town gave the new head coach his first Premier League win and lifted the Reds to fifth in the table.

Isak struck twice in the opening nine minutes at Portman Road to put the result beyond doubt before half-time, converting a near-post finish from Cody Gakpo’s first assist in the sixth minute before showing quick feet to round Kjell Scherpen and roll into an open goal three minutes later.

The goals are Isak’s second and third of the Premier League season, matching his entire tally from a difficult debut campaign at Anfield plagued by injury under Arne Slot.

The win arrived at a critical moment for Iraola, who had drawn his opening two matches and been under growing scrutiny following a chaotic summer. The Basque manager was clearly relieved in his post-match interviews.

“Definitely to get the first win. We needed that one with the way it has been. We got a clean sheet. Controlling the game quite well – I think that we started the game really strong, and then it was another kind of second half. Probably wasn’t as good as the first one,” he said.

Iraola on Isak: ‘My fight with him will be about other stuff’

Iraola was adamant about the quality Isak brings to this Liverpool side, while also revealing that his expectations of the striker extend well beyond the goals.

“He’s a massive player for us. My demands will probably not be about the goals, I know he is fit and in good shape. He’s going to produce the numbers.

“My fight with him will be more about other stuff, how to help the team in other situations, but it is good he has already played two full games, scoring the goals, so I am very happy to have him.

“Today I thought we were much better in our press in the first half, so we were covering very high and we could make contact with him in good positions. If we recover the ball lower, it will be harder to find him, so it’s all about a community effort to get our number nine in situations that he was in today.”

articles.title: Carrick says Dorgu is ‘like a new signing’ as Man United boss expresses delight with transfer window
articles.summary: United did not add a left-back in the summer window and made only four signings.
articles.content:
Carrick says Dorgu is ‘like a new signing’ as Man United boss expresses delight with transfer window

United did not add a left-back in the summer window and made only four signings.

Last Update:

Michael Carrick claimed he is delighted with Manchester United‘s business in the transfer window as he labelled Patrick Dorgu as being “like a new signing”.

United made only four senior signings in the transfer window, adding three midfielders in the form of Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba while bringing in Karl Darlow as a backup goalkeeper.

Yet the Red Devils still have an issue at left-back, where 31-year-old Luke Shaw will again be first choice, with 19-year-old Harry Amass the only other natural option at the position.

United’s decision not to sign a left-back in the transfer window has raised eyebrows, but Carrick pointed to Dorgu’s ability to operate there as he praised the winger’s potential impact after missing much of the second half of last season through a hamstring injury.

“He [Dorgu] can certainly play there [left-back],” Carrick told a pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday’s Premier League clash with Everton.

“He has done, without doubt. I’m not sitting here saying he can’t do that. It’s just the way we’ve been since I’ve been here.

“He actually has been injured, unfortunately, for some time. So, for me, he’s almost like a new player to have, and it’s almost like a new signing in some ways because he’s added so much to the group.

“He’s played off the right for Denmark, scored a great goal in the summer playing off the right in a forward position. He can play left-back.”

Though United’s business has attracted some criticism, Carrick made it clear he is more than satisfied.

“I think I’ve said it, we went in wanting to come out stronger from the group that we had last season, and we’ve definitely added to that,” he added.

“The situation is what it is, in terms of finances and what we can work with and what we’re trying to get the most of.

“Certainly, the players that we’ve brought into the group, I’m delighted with, absolutely delighted with. I think we’ve done some really good business there for the quality and the level of player that we’ve got. I’m really, really happy with that.”

articles.title: Maresca hails Fernandez’s winning mentality with record signing ready for Man City debut
articles.summary: Maresca says Fernandez is ready to face Coventry.
articles.content:
Maresca hails Fernandez’s winning mentality with record signing ready for Man City debut

Maresca says Fernandez is ready to face Coventry.

Last Update:

Enzo Maresca praised the winning mentality of Enzo Fernandez as Manchester City‘s record signing prepares to make his debut for the club.

The long-running transfer saga surrounding Fernandez came to a close on Tuesday as City completed a £125million deal with Chelsea to acquire the midfielder’s services.

That fee equalled the British record Liverpool paid to prise Alexander Isak from Newcastle United last summer.

City host newly promoted Coventry City on Saturday as they aim to make it three Premier League wins from three this season.

Maresca hails Fernandez mindset

While Fernandez will not be part of City’s leadership group, former Chelsea boss Maresca expects the Argentina star’s mindset to be crucial to their hopes of success going forward.

“I know Enzo quite well. I know what he can bring to the team,” Maresca told a pre-match press conference.

“He’s a winner and has a winning mentality. He knows how to win: World Cup, Club World Cup.

“The game before the window transfer closed, we had [Crystal] Palace away. That helped a lot because I was quite focused on that game. The day after, [the transfer] happened, and we were all happy.

“Enzo is ready [to play]. It’s important that he’s here with us. When you belong to a squad and another winner arrives, [players] are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four, five days, four or five players from the squad were asking ‘is he coming? Is he not? They want him to be with us.”

Fernandez became City’s ninth signing of the transfer window, with Maresca delighted with the backing he has received in the transfer market as he takes on the unenviable task of succeeding Pep Guardiola.

“It’s [the backing] very important. One of the main things in any football club is when the owner and the club support the manager,” he added.

“It’s a very good thing. I’m very, very happy for the effort from the ownership, [chairman] Khaldoon [Al Mubarak], [director of football] Hugo [Viana]. very happy. Now the squad is complete; it’s finished and it’s time to work.”

City also marked deadline day by bringing in winger Iliman Ndiaye from Everton in a £65m deal.

Maresca said of Ndiaye: “He’s so good. In the last two days, we can see already how good he is in terms of one-on-ones, the final third, inside the box. I’m very happy to have him.”

articles.title: ‘We have quality players in every position’ – Alonso happy with Chelsea squad despite lack of Fernandez replacement
articles.summary: The Blues' midfield is light on depth after the Argentina star's exit.
articles.content:
‘We have quality players in every position’ – Alonso happy with Chelsea squad despite lack of Fernandez replacement

The Blues' midfield is light on depth after the Argentina star's exit.

Last Update:

Xabi Alonso claims Chelsea have quality players at every position despite failing to fill the void left in their midfield by Enzo Fernandez’s departure.

Fernandez finally made his desired move to Manchester City on transfer deadline day, joining in a deal that saw City equal the British record by paying £125million for his services.

Chelsea thought they had sourced a replacement when they agreed a deal to sign Lamine Camara from Monaco, only for the Ligue 1 club to pull the plug on that transfer.

It has left the Blues looking light in the middle of the park, with Romeo Lavia, Moises Caicedo, Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson their four natural options in that position. Henderson remains sidelined with the injury he suffered at the World Cup.

Right-back Reece James also regularly plays in the engine room and will likely be required to do so more often following Fernandez’s exit.

But Alonso insisted he is happy with his squad as they prepare to face defending Premier League champions Arsenal on Sunday.

Asked about Fernandez’s move, Alonso told a pre-match press conference: “We take all the decisions together. We work together with big ones, small ones. We knew ultimately the goal is to have the best for the team. We want to build a good spirit, a good team.”

“In football many things happen. With Enzo we have had conversations and always with respect. What he has done for the club has been great, but now it’s time to move forward. We have players with quality in every position and now we are ready to go.

“We can be very happy with the whole transfer window. What we started talking about in May/early June – many things we have.

“It is a very balanced phase one we have made in this transfer window. Phase one is completed, it’s a good one for now and for the future.”

“I think that we are prepared and happy with the squad and the depth we have. It’s a good balance of players from different stages.

“We need to build that energy during the week to perform at the weekends. So far, it has been a good start and now we know who is in the building and it’s good to have that certainty.”

articles.title: Luis Enrique gives verdict on Barcola’s move from PSG to Liverpool
articles.summary: Barcola faced a lot of competition for places at PSG.
articles.content:
Luis Enrique gives verdict on Barcola’s move from PSG to Liverpool

Barcola faced a lot of competition for places at PSG.

Last Update:

Luis Enrique believes “everyone is a winner” from the move that saw Bradley Barcola leave Paris Saint-Germain to join Liverpool.

Barcola’s move to Anfield was completed on the penultimate day of the transfer window, the deal coming three years to the day of his switch from Lyon to PSG.

Liverpool paid an initial £106 million (€125m) to the Champions League holders, with the transfer featuring a further £17 million (€20m) in potential add-ons.

Barcola scored 39 goals in his time at the Parc des Princes but coach Luis Enrique conceded that, following PSG’s signings of fellow wingers Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts, he could no longer guarantee the 24-year-old the minutes he desired.

Speaking ahead of PSG’s home game against Monaco on Friday, Luis Enrique said: “Barcola grew enormously in Paris, but he also helped the team grow enormously.

“He wanted more playing time than I could guarantee him. In the end, I think everyone is a winner with that transfer. I truly wish him all the best.”

Barcola could make his debut for Liverpool when they visit Ipswich Town on Friday.

The Reds are still looking for their first win of the new Premier League season, having been held to 2-2 draws by Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest respectively.

Liverpool confirm signing of teenager N’Guessan

The move will become official in January.

Last Update:

Liverpool have confirmed the signing of teenage winger Djylian N’Guessan from Saint-Etienne.

The Reds announced the deal on Friday, with the 18-year-old set to officially join the club in January.

Having made 13 senior appearances for Ligue 2 leaders Saint-Etienne, N’Guessan will spend the 2026-27 season on loan at Ligue 1 Brest.

Brest visit Le Havre on Saturday, but N’Guessan may have a more high-profile debut next week, with the Pirates set to welcome Paris Saint-Germain to the Stade Francis-Le Blé next Sunday.

N’Guessan made seven appearances for France at last year’s Under-20 World Cup. He scored four goals at the 2025 Under-17 European Championship, earning a place in the Team of the Tournament as France lost the final to Portugal.

articles.title: Free agents XI: Players your club could still sign on a free transfer after closing of transfer window
articles.summary: Sancho, Pogba and Sterling are among the available free agent players
articles.content:
Free agents XI: Players your club could still sign on a free transfer after closing of transfer window

Sancho, Pogba and Sterling are among the available free agent players

Last Update:

An astonishing summer transfer window has finally come to an end, but a host of big-name stars are still available on transfers.

The likes of Jadon Sancho, Paul Pogba and Raheem Sterling are not contracted to any clubs and are available for free for any team, whether that be in the Premier League or eslewhere, which is willing to take a punt.

Read on for 101 Great Goals’ XI of the best free agents who your club could still move for.

Table of Contents

Goalkeeper: Sergio Rico (32)

Spaniard Sergio Rico is without a club after ending a two-year spell in Qatar with Al-Gharafa. Before that, Rico spent five years as understudy at Paris Saint-Germain and has also played for Sevilla and Fulham.

Right-back: Dani Carvajal (34)

A legendary figure at both Real Madrid and Spain, Dani Carvajal kept Trent Alexander-Arnold out of the side for much of last season and would surely be a shrewd addition on a free for a club’s right-back slot.

Centre-back: Sergio Ramos (40)

His former Real team-mate for several years is also available, with Sergio Ramos last playing football in 2025 for Monterrey. The four-time Champions League winner is yet to announce his retirement, so is technically still an available free agent.

Centre-back: David Alaba (34)

Injuries have massively disrupted the last few years of David Alaba’s career, with his Real Madrid contract expiring after making just 85 LaLiga appearances over six seasons.

Left-back: Oleksandr Zinchenko (29)

One of only two players under 30 in this list, Oleksandr Zinchenko has had a tough year since leaving Arsenal, struggling at Nottingham Forest before injuries limited to just two appearances on loan at Ajax.

Central midfield: Paul Pogba (33)

Once a world-record signing and a former World Cup winner, Paul Pogba is now a free agent after terminating his contract at Monaco a year early. Third spell at Manchester United, anyone?

Central midfield: Georginio Wijnaldum (35)

Instrumental in Liverpool’s years of success under Jurgen Klopp, Georginio Wijnaldum left Saudi Pro League side Al-Ettifaq this summer after three years.

Central midfield: Yves Bissouma (30)

Yves Bissouma was regarded as one of the Premier League’s brightest midfielders when he joined Tottenham for £30million in 2022, but has left North London as a free agent following a difficult 2025-26 season which saw them narrowly avoid relegation.

Right-wing: Riyad Mahrez (35)

Riyad Mahrez scored twice for Algeria at the World Cup but is now without a club after leaving Al-Ahli. The ex-Manchester City and Leicester star will go down as one of the Premier League’s greatest ever wingers but may now lack the dynamism and trickery needed to cut it back in England.

Striker: Karim Benzema (38)

After being replaced by Ollie Watkins at Al-Hilal, it remains to be seen whether Karim Benzema will prolong his successful playing career which saw him win the Ballon d’Or in 2022.

Left-wing: Jadon Sancho (26)

If you Jadon Sancho in 2021 when he joined Manchester United for £73m that he would be a free agent just five years later, he may think twice about making the move. Sancho failed to impress enough not only at Old Trafford but also on loan at Borussia Dortmund, Chelsea and Aston Villa, but there is still plenty of time to revive his career.

Substitutes

Dele Alli, Wilfried Zaha, James Rodriguez, Philippe Coutinho, Tyrell Malacia, Jamie Vardy, Anthony Martial, Chris Smalling

articles.title: FIFA accuses UEFA of ‘smear campaign’ against Infantino
articles.summary: FIFA has launched a fierce response to UEFA’s legal challenge over the abandoned plan to sell part of the World Cup to private investors, accusing European football’s governing body of waging a “smear campaign” against Gianni Infantino. The war between UEFA and the FIFA president has now escalated into the US courts, with UEFA seeking […]
articles.content:
FIFA accuses UEFA of ‘smear campaign’ against Infantino

Last Update:

FIFA has launched a fierce response to UEFA’s legal challenge over the abandoned plan to sell part of the World Cup to private investors, accusing European football’s governing body of waging a “smear campaign” against Gianni Infantino.

The war between UEFA and the FIFA president has now escalated into the US courts, with UEFA seeking evidence linked to the controversial FIFA Football Enterprises (FFE) project.

UEFA is also considering criminal proceedings against Infantino in Switzerland, adding another extraordinary twist to the growing battle for control of world football.

And FIFA has now hit back.

In a filing to a New York court, FIFA lawyers claimed UEFA’s legal applications were “little more than press releases” designed to further its alleged campaign against Infantino and the organisation’s leadership.

FIFA also questioned the basis of UEFA’s legal action, arguing that it is seeking evidence for a foreign criminal case that does not currently exist.

The latest development comes as UEFA looks to oust Infantino, either through his resignation or at the FIFA presidential election in March.

Table of Contents

FIFA defends controversial World Cup plan

At the heart of the dispute is the abandoned FIFA Football Enterprises proposal, which could have seen private investors pump billions into a new FIFA commercial subsidiary.

Up to $4.2bn was reportedly set to come from investors as part of the plans, with the wider venture valued at around $20bn.

The proposal sparked a huge backlash and was eventually abandoned.

Infantino’s senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro even labelled the deal a “bad deal” for football before quitting his position.

FIFA, however, insists the project was never a done deal.

Its lawyers argue that FFE was “only a proposal” and would have needed approval from FIFA’s member associations and the FIFA Council before going ahead.

The governing body has also accused UEFA of acting in its own financial interests.

“Rather than participate in that democratic process, UEFA issued a press release – the beginning of a weeks-long smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership,” FIFA claimed.

The filing goes even further, alleging that:

“UEFA’s economic motivation was to prevent smaller countries from having the financial strength to compete with the European elite.”

FIFA argues that giving smaller nations greater financial resources would ultimately make world football more competitive – potentially weakening UEFA’s grip on the global game.

“If soccer is strengthened in the developing world, global competition increases,” FIFA said, arguing that this would “reduce UEFA’s market power” and create greater competition for its flagship tournaments.

UEFA vs Infantino gets uglier

The latest legal salvo marks another dramatic escalation in the increasingly bitter relationship between UEFA and Infantino.

UEFA has already warned that it could pursue criminal proceedings against the FIFA president in Switzerland, while also seeking evidence from individuals linked to the proposed investment deal.

The FIFA filing does not directly address all of UEFA’s criticism of Infantino, nor does it respond to concerns raised by football confederations in Asia and North America, which have accused the FIFA president of a “fundamental breach of trust.”

For now, the battle is firmly in the courts.

But with the FIFA presidential election looming in March, the fight over Infantino’s future – and the direction of world football – looks set to become even more explosive.

articles.title: Liverpool: Ismaila Sarr ‘needs time’ to ‘digest’ failed move
articles.summary: Sarr looked set to join Liverpool before the transfer deadline
articles.content:
Liverpool: Ismaila Sarr ‘needs time’ to ‘digest’ failed move

Sarr looked set to join Liverpool before the transfer deadline

Last Update:

Ismaila Sarr will “need time” to “digest” his failed move to Liverpool, Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage says.

Sarr, who was Palace’s top scorer last season with 21 goals, emerged as a late target for the Reds during the closing days of the summer transfer window, and it looked as though the Senegal international may be closing in on a move to Anfield as they looked to bolster their wide options.

But the move did not materialise before the deadline, ensuring he will remain at Selhurst Park until at least January.

Sage admitted: “He has to digest for sure because it’s a dream for a lot of players to play with this kind of club.

“He had a good opportunity but in the end it didn’t work. If he wants to continue, you have to have a good season with us as he did last year. We know he needs time.

“Like every bad situation, time does the job and we need time for that.”

Palace gave their best to sign Fofana

The 28-year-old has not featured in either of the Eagles’ first two Premier League games against Everton and Manchester City amid speculation over his future, although it was deemed he had a thigh injury that will also keep him out of their clash with Fulham this weekend.

Palace were reportedly lining up a late move to try and hijack Sunderland’s move for Malick Fofana, who Sage managed at Lyon, but the 21-year-old chose to move to the North East instead.

“We gave our best,” added Frenchman Sage on the negotiations. “At the end of the day the player chose his criteria and I wish him and them the best because he’s a good guy and a good player.”

Palace, like Saturday’s opponents Fulham, are still searching for their first Premier League points of the season after losing to Eveton and Man City so far.

articles.title: Tottenham omit Richarlison from Premier League squad amid Trabzonspor interest
articles.summary: Richarlison has reportedly agreed to move to Turkey.
articles.content:
Tottenham omit Richarlison from Premier League squad amid Trabzonspor interest

Richarlison has reportedly agreed to move to Turkey.

Last Update:

Tottenham have omitted Richarlison from their Premier League squad.

The Brazilian forward is in the final year of his contract in North London and was left out of last Saturday’s 2-0 defeat to Newcastle United, with Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi saying the 29-year-old had “asked too many times to leave”.

Richarlison had looked set to return to former club Everton in the final days of the Premier League transfer window, with Iliman Ndiaye going the other way.

That deal did not come to fruition, but Richarlison has been handed a potential exit route, with reports claiming he has agreed to join Turkish side Trabzonspor. The Turkish transfer window remains open until Friday.

Tottenham are said to have informed Richarlison of their decision before the Premier League transfer deadline to allow him to find a new club.

Richarlison has scored 32 goals for Tottenham since joining from Everton in 2022.

Amid the speculation surrounding his future, Richarlison released an explosive statement on Monday.

In a post on his Instagram story, Richarlison wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in the last few years, I’ve decided that never again will anyone decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things, and almost all of them happened because decisions were made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through far worse, believe me.

“I’ve always made it clear, every time I had the chance, that leaving for another club would only happen if it was also good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it. Just like I didn’t accept it when everything was going badly and they needed me.

“I stayed and gave everything. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect I’ve always shown Spurs and everyone who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.

“If they reach an agreement between Spurs and Everton, I will return to my beloved club. My intention was to go back to the place where I was very happy, yes, but the negotiations happened only in the way certain people wanted, and it will no longer be like that.

“Despite all this turmoil, I am under contract at Spurs and will remain at the club’s disposal.”

With Richarlison no longer at Spurs’ disposal following their decision, Omar Marmoush and Dominic Solanke will be their senior options in the central striker role for the remainder of the campaign.

Tottenham are winless after two Premier League games despite committing a huge transfer outlay in a bid to turn around their fortunes after narrowly avoiding relegation last season.

The transfer window closed on Tuesday with Tottenham having spent £394million. They visit Nottingham Forest on Saturday in a bid to claim their first league win of the new season.

articles.title: Martinelli completes £60m move from Arsenal to Al Hilal
articles.summary: Martinelli's seven-year stay at Emirates Stadium is over.
articles.content:
Martinelli completes £60m move from Arsenal to Al Hilal

Martinelli's seven-year stay at Emirates Stadium is over.

Last Update:

Gabriel Martinelli has completed his move from Arsenal to Al Hilal.

The £60million transfer, which is subject to the completion of regulatory processes, sees the Brazil forward end his seven-year stay with the Gunners.

In that time Martinelli has won three trophies, making 30 appearances in the Premier League last season as Arsenal won the title for the first time since 2004.

The 25-year-old scored only once in the Premier League in 2025-26 but was more prolific in the Champions League, netting six times and providing two assists as Arsenal reached the final, where they lost to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties.

Martinelli also won the FA Cup and the Community Shield during his career in North London.

Having joined from Ituano in 2019, Martinelli scored 62 goals in 278 appearances for Arsenal.

However, he was not included in the squad for this year’s Community Shield win over Manchester City, nor did he feature in the match day group for the Premier League wins over Coventry City and Aston Villa.

Now he will join an Al Hilal side that sit joint-top of the Saudi Pro League having claimed four wins from four to start the new season.

Martinelli is the third former Premier League player to join Al Hilal during the Saudi transfer window, which does not close until October 12. They also signed Ollie Watkins from Villa and Crysencio Summerville from West Ham.

articles.title: ‘This is something I like as a coach’ – Jaissle praises key Fernandez-Pardo trait as Newcastle boss explains Woltemade loan
articles.summary: Matthias Jaissle says Matias Fernandez-Pardo needs time to adapt
articles.content:
‘This is something I like as a coach’ – Jaissle praises key Fernandez-Pardo trait as Newcastle boss explains Woltemade loan

Matthias Jaissle says Matias Fernandez-Pardo needs time to adapt

Last Update:

Matthias Jaissle praised the versatility of Newcastle United deadline day signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo as the head coach cautioned the forward will need time to adapt to the Premier League.

Fernandez-Pardo became Newcastle’s eighth signing of a transfer window that saw their squad undergo a substantial revamp as they agreed a £51million deal with Lille to sign the Belgium international on a five-year deal.

The 21-year-old has can play as a number nine, a number 10 and on both wings, and it is that flexibility that Jaissle, who is unbeaten in his first three games after replacing Eddie Howe in August, appears to value most.

Previewing Bournemouth’s visit on Saturday, Jaissle said: “We worked hard on the deal, finalised it in the last hours and we’re really pleased.

“For a young age, he is already showing a lot of strength on the pitch. His physical levels are really strong for our idea of how we want to play football.

“That speed up front can cause many problems. He is versatile, which gives us the freedom to adjust from match to match. This is something I like as a coach, that we are flexible.”

Fernandez-Pardo has not played 90 minutes in a game since his final match for Lille on May 17.

As such, Jaissle indicated Newcastle may have to build up his minutes, and believes patience will be needed with Fernandez-Pardo and several of their summer signings, all of whom are 24 or under.

“He is fit and training with us,” Jaissle added. “It has been a while since he played a full 90 minutes so it is also, for a young lad, important to adapt towards our intensity in training but also in the Premier League.

“We will have a close eye on him and be smart with the load management.

“With these signings, with young players, they need time. They need time to adapt. Yes, there are players [who] adapted now really fast, but there will be ups and downs with young players. This is something we know and we will support them in the lows, but also the highs.

“We have a squad with huge potential and, therefore, we are really happy.”

Jaissle confident Woltemade can shine at Juventus

As Fernandez-Pardo arrived, another forward left St. James’ Park, with Nick Woltemade joining Juventus on a season-long loan.

Woltemade signed Newcastle in a club-record deal worth £69million, but the Germany international has struggled to cement a role in the side after initially making a red-hot start to his career on Tyneside.

But Jaissle has high hopes Woltemade can excel in Turin.

“I really appreciate Nick as a player, for his quality on the pitch but I also appreciate him as a human being,” said Jaissle.

“We always have good conversations, really honest conversations and he has decided now to take another challenge. Hopefully, it goes well.

“I’m really optimistic that he will shine there, he will score a lot of goals there for sure. He’s still our player so, therefore, we will make sure we stay in close contact.”

The Newcastle boss also addressed rumours from Denmark that striker Will Osula, who has missed the last two games with a foot injury sustained in the season opener with Liverpool, is facing an extended absence.

Jaissle said: “I don’t know if the Danish journalists have more information than I have, I doubt it.”

articles.title: Argentina to pause league matches following Messi international retirement
articles.summary: Messi announced the end of his Argentina career on Monday
articles.content:
Argentina to pause league matches following Messi international retirement

Messi announced the end of his Argentina career on Monday

Last Update:

Argentina will pause all men’s and women’s matches in the 10th minute this weekend for a minute’s applause following Lionel Messi’s decision to retire from international football.

On Monday, Messi announced the end of his Argentina career, having set the record for caps (207) and goals (125) for his country.

Messi helped Argentina to three World Cup finals, finally lifting the trophy in 2022 as they beat France on penalties, though a 1-0 defeat to Spain in this year’s showpiece denied them a successful defence of the crown.

Prior to success at the World Cup in Qatar, Messi lifted his first international trophy with Argentina in 2021 as they ended a 28-year wait for Copa America glory. They subsequently retained that title in 2024.

Only the late Diego Maradona can rival Messi in the realm of Argentina legends, and the country’s football association (AFA) announced the special tribute to him on Thursday.

A statement from the AFA read: “In tribute and homage to Lionel Messi’s career with the Argentina national team, at the 10th minute of play in all matches the referees will stop the game and a general minute of applause will be held.

“We look forward to seeing you on the fields – join us in this recognition!”

Lionel Messi: Argentina icon’s retirement statement

“After all this time that has passed since the final, and after much thought, I want to announce to everyone that I am retiring from the national team,” Messi said.

“It was a decision that hurt – and still hurts – to my core, but I understand that it’s the right time.

“I swear that I always gave my all – not just in the last few years when we won everything, but before that, too.

“I always fought and gave everything for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you proud to be Argentinian through football.

“There’s not much time left and chapters are closing, and this is one that hurts me deeply. I love, loved, and will always love being on the national team.

“I’ve given everything I have; I have nothing more to give and, besides, there are some great young players coming up behind me who deserve to be there.”

articles.title: Dzeko announces retirement from international football
articles.summary: Dzeko is Bosnia's record cap holder and scorer
articles.content:
Dzeko announces retirement from international football

Dzeko is Bosnia's record cap holder and scorer

Last Update:

Edin Dzeko has announced his retirement from international football.

The 40-year-old Bosnia-Herzegovina international has won 151 caps and scored 73 goals for his country, with both tallies standing as a records.

He featured at the 2026 World Cup finals this summer, helping Bosnia reach the knockout rounds for the first time in their history as an independent nation. They were eliminated in the round of 32 by United States.

In a statement released on social media, Dzeko confirmed he will make his final appearance for Bosnia when they face Sweden in Zenica on October 2 in the UEFA Nations League.

Dzeko to say farewell against Sweden

Dzeko scored a key goal against Wales in the play-offs of UEFA qualifying for the World Cup this year, his strike forcing a penalty shoot-out that Bosnia won to set up a final with Italy, in which they again prevailed on spot-kicks to book their place in the finals.

And Dzeko identified the pair of World Cup qualifications as two of the proudest moments of his career as he confirmed the end of his time in the international game.

The former Manchester City and Inter Milan striker wrote: “Sometimes I found myself wondering when this moment would come, but I never imagined how emotional I would feel writing these words.

“On October 2nd, against Sweden, I will play my next and final match for our national team.

“Nothing in my career has ever compared to the pride I have felt every single time I wore that shirt. Nothing.

“It was my childhood dream, a dream I carried with me on each of the 151 occasions I had the honour of representing my country on a football pitch.

“I was always proud to do so, just as I was the first time. Almost 20 years have passed since that match against Turkey.  So many things have changed, and I have changed too, but my love for this shirt never has.

“Now I feel the time has come to step aside. If I have made it to the age of 40 with the national team, it is because I truly gave everything I had. Every time. Everything.

“Playing for my country has been the most emotional opportunity football has ever given me.

A post shared by Edin Dzeko (@edindzeko)

“Qualifying for our first World Cup in 2014 remains one of the happiest moments of my life as a footballer.

“The emotions I felt on the night of the goal against Wales, and then in Zenica against Italy in March, will stay in my heart forever.

“Seeing my people celebrating in the streets of our cities was another incredible gift that football has given me.

“There will be time to thank everyone who has been by my side and supported me throughout this wonderful journey.

“For now, I just hope you will be there that night against Sweden, so we can share one more emotion…Because every one of these incredible moments has been something we have lived together.

“And that is how I want to experience my final night representing my country: with all of you by my side, wearing the shirt I have loved since I was a boy – and the shirt I will love for the rest of my life.”

articles.title: Iraola ‘honest’ over failed Gakpo deal: ‘He was well aware of the situation’
articles.summary: Cody Gakpo joined Liverpool from PSV in 2023
articles.content:
Iraola ‘honest’ over failed Gakpo deal: ‘He was well aware of the situation’

Cody Gakpo joined Liverpool from PSV in 2023

Last Update:

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola says he has been “honest since the beginning” with Cody Gakpo after the Netherlands international’s £85 million move to Manchester City fell through late on transfer deadline day.

The Reds were widely reported to have rejected City’s offer because they had not been able to sign a replacement for the wide forward, who scored nine goals in all competitions last season and put Liverpool ahead in their 2-2 draw at Newcastle in their season opener on August 23.

“He was well aware of the situation in the market,” said Iraola. “We were constantly talking with each other.

“Cody is a very smart player. My relationship with him has been honest since the beginning. He has performed very well in all the pre-season [and league] games.

“He has trained very well and I hope we keep him at the same level. He is in a good place physically and mentally. I am glad to keep Cody because he is a valuable player.”

Table of Contents

Liverpool squad: What Iraola said about right wing

Iraola, who made bids for wingers including Brighton & Hove Albion’s Yankuba Minteh, pointed out that he has been operating with the likes of new left-winger Victor Munoz, Gakpo and prospect Rio Ngumoha on the right.

“I have seen them [play well] on the right,” he added. “Rio is probably more specific to the left side, but he has the willingness to improve and play on the right side.”

Bradley Barcola: New Liverpol signing ‘priority’

Liverpool signed Bradley Barcola – a right-footed left-sided forward – for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain on Monday.

“He is very open and I think he can play right and left,” suggested Iraola. “He started on the right side when he [was] with Lyon and it will depend on the match-ups, but I am happy with the wingers we have in those positions.

“[Barcola] was our priority, let’s say – to sign a very, very good player in that position.

“He has come with the right mentality. I liked from him that he wanted Liverpool a lot. He just wanted to come here and that is a good first sign, being the player he is [with] the things that he has won.”

Ipswich Town vs Liverpool: Barcola ‘available’

Having followed up that result at Newcastle by drawing 2-2 at home to Nottingham Forest on Saturday, Liverpool will seek their first competitive win under Iraola by visiting Premier League newcomers Ipswich Town on Friday.

Barcola could make his debut against opponents who beat Sunderland 2-1 at home in their opener but lost 5-2 at Manchester United on Sunday.

“He has come with the willingness to help us,” Iraola said of Barcola. “I am very happy with him and he trained well with us.

“It’s true he hasn’t had minutes in pre-season but he has been training and it’s a decision we have to make.

“If everything goes well in training [on Thursday], he will definitely be available.

“We need a win. We are frustrated with this part of the job… I want to win, I need to win.

“The first two gameweeks were probably the most difficult ones, in terms of the market being open.

“Now I am much more comfortable. The market has closed and we know who we are. We have a lot of talent. Now we have to perform and do our job. We will start [against Ipswich].”

articles.title: Kane scores for Bayern as holders start with cup win
articles.summary: England captain is off the mark for the new season
articles.content:
Kane scores for Bayern as holders start with cup win

England captain is off the mark for the new season

Last Update:

Holders Bayern Munich got their DFB Pokal run off to a winning start with Harry Kane on target in a 4-1 win against second tier Osnabruck.

Kane, who scored a hat-trick when Bayern won the cup final against Stuttgart in May, drew them level with his first goal of the season after Robin Meisner had given the hosts a shock lead.

Tom Bischof put Bayern ahead before the break and Michael Olise grabbed a third in the second half before Kane struck a late penalty.

Jamal Musiala was not included in Bayern’s squad as the Germany star remained absent since collapsing in two pre-season games because of a neurological issue.

Bayern coach Vincent Kompany said Musiala “might” be an option for Bayern’s league game against promoted Schalke on Saturday.

“But I don’t want to put any more pressure on the guy,” Kompany said.

The hosts stunned the reigning champions inside five minutes. A long clearance caused confusion in the Bayern backline and Meisner pounced, lashing an audacious first-time volley into the top corner past Jonas Urbig to ignite the home crowd.

Bayern responded before the 20-minute mark via a familiar source. Joshua Kimmich floated a pinpoint ball over the top into the penalty area, forcing Robin Fabinski into an awkward headed clearance that popped up into the air. Kane reacted instantly, executing a difficult half-volley into the back of the net to level the tie. The strike saw Kane equal a club record by scoring in his seventh consecutive DFB-Pokal match.

Young midfielder Bischof followed in when Luis Díaz’s initial drive was parried by goalkeeper Jonas Krumrey, and Olise got the third after second-half substitute Lennart Karl seized upon a loose pass to pick him out.

Kane then buried a penalty with four minutes left before being replaced.

Bayern have won the German cup on 21 occasions, but had gone six years without a win before last season’s triumph.

articles.title: McTominay talks Ferguson bond, Mourinho call and heart surgery
articles.summary: Scotland's Scott McTominay is set to miss Champions League games
articles.content:
McTominay talks Ferguson bond, Mourinho call and heart surgery

Scotland's Scott McTominay is set to miss Champions League games

Last Update:

Scott McTominay says he would consider a call from Jose Mourinho if an offer came to join Real Madrid, while sharing that he remains in touch with Sir Alex Ferguson as he prepares to undergo heart surgery.

Speaking to Corriere della Sera, the Napoli midfielder opened up about the mentors who shaped his career at Manchester United.

When asked how he would respond if Mourinho – who handed him his Premier League debut at United in 2017 – called to bring him to Real Madrid, McTominay admitted:

“If that happened, I’d think about it.”

The Scotland international also confirmed he still maintains a connection with legendary United boss Sir Alex Ferguson.

“I last spoke to him on the phone a year ago. He’s a very busy man, but I’m sure he’d help me if I needed anything.”

Table of Contents

Minor heart procedure ahead

McTominay is set to undergo ablation surgery to treat a benign arrhythmia and regulate his heartbeat. The procedure means the 29-year-old will miss Napoli’s high-profile encounters against Inter and Arsenal in the Champions League, although he is expected to return after the international break in late September.

Asked whether he felt concerned about the diagnosis, McTominay remained defiant:

“No, it’s a problem I have to deal with. I just found out about the operation. But we’ll see each other soon, very soon. Stronger than before.”

MCTOMINAY!! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿UNBELIEVABLE! 😲#BBCFootball pic.twitter.com/F0IFFjU49e

Big fixtures, managers and life in Naples

McTominay was quick to back Napoli ahead of their trip to Inter this weekend and says the squad are coping well with the transition from Antonio Conte to Massimiliano Allegri.

He said: “They’re different coaches. Conte was very tactically oriented, and we trained a lot. I had two wonderful years with him.

“He’s extraordinary, a serial winner. Only time will tell how things will go with the new coach, but so far he’s a good guy and has good tactical ideas.

“We just need time to implement them and play a little better.”

articles.summary: Trabzonspor host Hearts in the Conference League
articles.content:
Manager leaves Trabzonspor weeks after signing Salah

Trabzonspor host Hearts in the Conference League

Last Update:

Trabzonspor have parted company with head coach Fatih Tekke by mutual consent, plunging the Turkish heavyweights into chaos less than a month after pulling off the blockbuster signing of Mohamed Salah.

Tekke, who took charge in March 2025 and guided the club to Turkish Cup glory last season, tendered his resignation last week following an embarrassing 5-0 aggregate drubbing against Hungarian outfit Ferencvaros in the UEFA Europa League play-offs.

While the board initially rejected Tekke resignation to keep stability, Monday’s dismal 2-1 Super Lig defeat at promoted Amedspor proved the final straw, prompting the hierarchy to act.

Mohamed Salah, @SuperLig’e merhaba dedi! 👋#TrendyolSüperLig | @Trabzonspor | @MoSalah pic.twitter.com/zJKXe7jGGg

Table of Contents

How have Trabzonspor started the 2026/27 season?

The Black Sea Storm invested heavily this summer, headlined by landing 34-year-old Liverpool icon Salah as a free agent on a two-year deal worth a reported €17m (£14.6m) per season.

Trabzonspor have also signed a former Reds team-mate of Salah in Brazil midfielder Fabinho.

While Salah has delivered individually by scoring three goals in his first four appearances across all competitions, the team have not performed.

With just four points from their opening three league fixtures and an exit from Europe’s second-tier competition, the pressure became insurmountable.

Trabzonspor fixtures: Conference League 2026/27

Tekke is not the only departure in Trabzon. Rangers and Sheffield United midfielder John Lundstram, who spent last season on loan at Hull City, has had his contract terminated two years after arriving in Turkiye.

Crashing out of the Europa League has dropped Trabzonspor into the league phase of the UEFA Conference League, starting with a trip to Finnish side Kups on October 15, followed by the visit of Scottish Premiership team Heart of Midlothian to the Papara Park on October 22.

Hearts will now be bracing to face a side possessing Salah’s firepower, but likely operating under an entirely new managerial setup.

articles.title: Carragher: Arsenal lack ’10 out of 10′ player
articles.summary: Jamie Carragher says Arsenal lack an outstanding player in attack
articles.content:
Carragher: Arsenal lack ’10 out of 10′ player

Jamie Carragher says Arsenal lack an outstanding player in attack

Last Update:

Arsenal failed to make a “10 out of 10” attacking signing during the transfer window, according to Jamie Carragher.

The reigning Premier League champions explored ambitious moves for Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior and Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez but were unable to complete either deal.

Christos Tzolis was Arsenal’s only attacking addition, joining from Club Brugge for £34m.

The Gunners also saw Leandro Trossard leave for Besiktas, Gabriel Jesus join Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri move to Borussia Dortmund. Gabriel Martinelli is also in talks over a move to Al Hilal, whose transfer window remains open.

Carragher believes Arsenal already have plenty of good attacking options but were missing a player capable of taking their attack to another level.

“They have got really good strikers. I like Kai Havertz and I think Mikel Arteta likes him, as well,” Carragher said on Sky Sports.

“Viktor Gyokeres has been what most people felt he would be when he came – not quite elite but he can still score goals in certain games. They can still use him to do that job this season.

“They needed someone to be a gamechanger. They tried to get Vinicius Junior, they tried to get Alvarez – that’s the calibre of players.”

Arsenal have built one of the strongest squads in the Premier League, meaning Carragher believes only a world-class addition would significantly improve Arteta’s team.

“It’s very hard to improve Arsenal now because they are such a good team, such a strong squad,” he added.

“So you’re talking about a world-class player as the only one that can improve them. They’ve tried to get them and haven’t been able to get these deals over the line.

“There’s no point bringing somebody of the level that they’ve already got. They’ve got five or six players in attack which I would call ‘seven or eight out of 10 players’.

“They wanted a ‘nine or 10 out of 10 player’ but couldn’t get it across the line.”

articles.title: Femi Azeez transfer: Brighton sign Millwall winger for £15m
articles.summary: Femi Azeez is Brighton's 11th summer signing
articles.content:
Femi Azeez transfer: Brighton sign Millwall winger for £15m

Femi Azeez is Brighton's 11th summer signing

Last Update:

Femi Azeez has playfully told Brighton & Hove Albion he is “sorry” about their wait for the winger to join the Premier League club after signing from Millwall for a fee that could exceed £15 million.

Albion announced the arrival of Azeez, 25, well after the transfer deadline of 23:00 BST on Tuesday because the Seagulls had completed the deal sheet by then, concluding Millwall’s club-record sale by the extended deadline of 01:00 on Wednesday.

“Sorry to keep you waiting,” the Nigeria international told fans in a clip released on Wednesday morning showing him arriving at Albion’s training ground and posing in the club’s home shirt.

The wait is over. 😏 pic.twitter.com/06Cg0YI85g

Table of Contents

Femi Azeez stats: ‘Strong desire’ to leave Millwall for Brighton

Brighton will pay an initial £12.5m for Azeez, who joined the Lions from Reading in 2024 and scored 14 goals in 77 appearances for the Championship promotion hopefuls.

“Femi expressed a strong desire to depart the club this window in pursuit of Premier League football, which The Lions have reluctantly agreed to accept,” Millwall said in a statement, thanking Azeez for a spell that included 11 goals and eight assists in 37 games last season and a place in the PFA Championship team of the year.

Albion Sporting Director Mike Cave said Azeez had been “one of the most exciting attacking talents in the Championship” during Millwall’s run to last season’s play-offs.

Brighton beat Aston Villa at home before losing at Chelsea on Sunday in their second league match of 2026/27.

Millwall beat Bristol City away and Norwich City at home in the second tier but lost 5-1 at Southampton on Saturday.

When does the summer transfer window 2026 close?

The window opened on Monday June 15 and shut on Tuesday September 1.

After that, every Premier League club can register a squad of up to 25 players, 17 of whom are allowed to be non-Home Grown Players.

A Home Grown Player has been registered with any club affiliated to the English or Welsh Football Association for three entire seasons or 36 months across their career before his 21st birthday, or the end of the season during which they turn 21.

Under-21 players do not count towards the 25-man limit.

How does Premier League transfer window extension work?

Clubs can have an extra two hours to file the remaining documentation if they submit a deal sheet confirming that an agreement has been reached.

The deal sheet must arrive fully completed before the transfer window closes.

For international transfers, clubs also have to comply with the FIFA Transfer Matching System deadline of midnight.

When was transfer deadline day around Europe?

There are slight variations between the major European leagues. Here’s when the summer transfer windows shut.

When does the 2026/27 winter transfer window open?

The Premier League winter transfer window opens on Friday January 1, 2027 and closes on Monday February 1, 2027 at 23:00 BST.

Can Premier League clubs sign players outside of the window?

Clubs can only add players outside of transfer windows who are free agents and if they have room in their 25-man squad.

Premier League teams can still announce deals with other clubs, but those players will not be registered to play until the window re-opens.

This means there is usually little to no movement when the window closes, with four months to wait until the window re-opens.

Players can be released by Premier League clubs at any time, but the usual rule is that they cannot sign for another side outside of the market.

articles.title: Watkins claims Saudi Pro League is ‘Premier League quality’ after debut goal
articles.summary: Ollie Watkins scored on his debut for Al-Hilal.
articles.content:
Watkins claims Saudi Pro League is ‘Premier League quality’ after debut goal

Ollie Watkins scored on his debut for Al-Hilal.

Last Update:

Ollie Watkins marked his Al-Hilal debut with a goal in their 3-0 home win over Al-Ahli in the Saudi Pro League on Tuesday before describing the standard of football in Saudi Arabia as “Premier League quality”.

The England international joined Al-Hilal from Aston Villa last week and came off the bench in the second half before scoring with a back-post header in the closing stages.

Ollie Watkins opens his RSL goal count on his debut for Al Hilal 🔵 pic.twitter.com/T9KWKlZc09

Sergej Savic opened the scoring for Al-Hilal before former West Ham forward Crysencio Summerville doubled their advantage.

Watkins left Villa after six years at the club, scoring 108 goals in 278 appearances and helping the Villans win the Europa League last season.

The 30-year-old was one of several key departures from Villa this summer, with Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne also leaving. Watkins, however, was the only player to move outside Europe.

“The level I saw here today was honestly of Premier League quality,” Watkins said after the game.

“The match was very strong physically and demanding, and the quality was extremely high.

“I knew straight away [to join Al Hilal when the offer came]. I watched the [FIFA] Club World Cup and I saw how well they performed. I always see who’s at the top of the league and they’re always up there.

“And look, I want to come here. I want to win trophies and I think this team is going to give me the best possible chance of doing that.”

Watkins aiming to score in every game

Watkins also set himself the target of scoring in every game after getting off the mark on his debut.

“I want to score in every game,” he added.

“But I kept going, kept going, and I’m going to get a lot of chances. Ruben Neves and Sergej Milinkovic-Savic are very intelligent players and all I need to do is make the run.

“I’m a bit rusty at the moment, only had a couple of days training so, once I get in the groove, I’m going to be good.”

Watkins also had a goal ruled out for offside shortly before finding the net.

“I kept going and obviously just before [my goal] I got called offside, which was disappointing,” he said.

articles.title: Players set to wear debut patches during Champions League this season
articles.summary: Players will wear debut patches in the Champions League as part of an agreement with Fanatics.
articles.content:
Players set to wear debut patches during Champions League this season

Players will wear debut patches in the Champions League as part of an agreement with Fanatics.

Last Update:

Debut patches will feature in the men’s Champions League for the first time during the 2026/27 season as part of a new agreement between Fanatics and UEFA.

Players making their first appearance in the competition will wear a small patch on the sleeve of their shirt featuring the word “debut” alongside the Champions League starball logo.

After the match, the patch will be removed and sent to Topps, the trading card company owned by Fanatics. It will then be incorporated into a unique trading card that will also be signed by the player.

Players who make their Champions League debut as substitutes will be eligible for a patch, while those named in a matchday squad but left unused will have to wait until they make their first appearance.

The Champions League is Europe’s premier club competition, with 36 teams qualifying through their domestic league campaigns or by winning the Europa League.

The debut patch programme is expected to be introduced in the Women’s Champions League from the 2027/28 season.

Fanatics has already used the initiative across several major sports. The programme originated in Major League Baseball before expanding to the NFL, NBA, Bundesliga, Formula 1, MLS, UFC and WWE.

The Champions League initiative is the latest collaboration between Fanatics, Topps and UEFA as the companies look to create new collectable items around European club football.

articles.title: Balogun pulls plug on Everton move after medical issues
articles.summary: Folarin Balogun opted to stay at Monaco despite a move to Everton being agreed.
articles.content:
Balogun pulls plug on Everton move after medical issues

Folarin Balogun opted to stay at Monaco despite a move to Everton being agreed.

Last Update:

Everton’s move for Folarin Balogun collapsed after the striker changed his mind about joining the club following a medical at their Finch Farm training base.

Issues identified during the medical led Everton and Monaco to renegotiate the initial £40m deal for the 25-year-old striker.

The United States international and both clubs had signed a deal sheet before the 23:00 BST transfer deadline, but Balogun subsequently had a change of heart and walked away from the move.

Balogun had emerged as a late target for Everton after Guinea-Bissau striker Beto completed a permanent transfer to Serie A club Fiorentina.

The Toffees also explored moves for Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee and Aston Villa forward Tammy Abraham, but were unable to convince either player to join.

Everton did complete the signing of Jack Grealish from Manchester City on a season-long loan on transfer deadline day.

Grealish returns to Merseyside

Grealish spent the 2025-26 season on loan at Everton, making 20 appearances before suffering a season-ending foot injury in January.

The 30-year-old had attracted interest from several clubs, including boyhood club Aston Villa, but opted to reunite with David Moyes on Merseyside.

“I think I’m at my best at everything in life, not just football, when I feel loved. That’s what the manager has given me, what my team-mates have given me and especially what the fans have given me,” Grealish said.

“Every time I see an Everton fan, it’s just pure love and the way they’ve welcomed me since that first game against Leeds, I’ll never forget that.”

Everton also completed the signing of Ainsley Maitland-Niles from French side Lyon.

The 29-year-old former Arsenal player has won five England caps and can operate at full-back or in midfield.

articles.title: Chelsea’s Camara deal collapses overnight as Blues left without Fernandez replacement
articles.summary: Chelsea were left stunned in the transfer market overnight.
articles.content:
Chelsea’s Camara deal collapses overnight as Blues left without Fernandez replacement

Chelsea were left stunned in the transfer market overnight.

Last Update:

Lamine Camara will remain at Monaco after his proposed £47.1m move to Chelsea collapsed after the transfer deadline.

The 22-year-old Senegal midfielder completed a medical in France on Tuesday evening, but Chelsea’s move fell through shortly after the 23:00 BST deadline.

Chelsea had already seen two bids rejected by Monaco before the Ligue 1 club lowered their asking price when Folarin Balogun’s proposed move to Everton came into renewed doubt.

Chelsea were confident the deal for Camara would be completed and had already sanctioned Enzo Fernandez’s joint-British record £125m transfer to Manchester City in anticipation of the Senegal international arriving.

However, Chelsea were left furious after being informed in writing by Monaco that the deal for Camara would not go ahead.

The Premier League club say they were given no explanation for the decision, although sources suggest that they believe Monaco’s stance was influenced by Everton’s proposed move for United States international Balogun.

Chelsea left stunned

Chelsea had initially struggled to reach an agreement with Monaco for Camara, but made progress when reports emerged that Balogun’s move to Everton was in doubt.

Sources in France had claimed Monaco needed to make a major sale this summer and preferred to cash in on Balogun.

Camara played in Monaco’s 2-0 win over Marseille on Sunday, while Balogun was left out of the squad.

However, as doubts grew over Balogun’s proposed move to Everton, Monaco’s asking price for Camara appeared to fall, allowing Chelsea to agree a deal worth around £47m.

Once Balogun’s transfer appeared to be back on track, Monaco appeared to change their position and decided against allowing Camara to leave.

articles.title: Man City complete British-record move for ‘complete midfielder’ Fernandez
articles.summary: Fernandez reunites with Enzo Maresca.
articles.content:
Man City complete British-record move for ‘complete midfielder’ Fernandez

Fernandez reunites with Enzo Maresca.

Last Update:

Manchester City have completed the signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea in a deal that equals the British record.

Fernandez arrives at the Etihad Stadium for a fee of £125million, matching the amount Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak last summer.

As was the case with that deal, City’s pursuit of Fernandez went right to the last day of the window, but it has ended with them getting the final piece of the puzzle in terms of the revamp of their midfield.

Fernandez becomes City’s ninth signing of the summer and the third midfielder they have added to their ranks following the acquisitions of Elliot Anderson for £116m and Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for £86m.

Former midfielder lynchpin Rodri left to join Barcelona, with Nico Gonzalez moving to Newcastle and Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders signing for Real Madrid and Al Qadsiah respectively.

Table of Contents

Fernandez ‘could not be happier’ with City move

City will now look for Fernandez to form a fearsome combination with Anderson and Bouaddi after reuniting him with former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca.

And Fernandez promised to give everything to make sure that proves to be the case.

“Manchester City are the most successful club in England in recent times,” he told the club’s official website.

“Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are.

“I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

“If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.

“I pride myself on continually improving my game. Anyone who’s worked with me will know how hard I train every single day and how much I put into matches. I give absolutely everything and I can promise Manchester City that will continue now I’m here.

“I want to thank Hugo [Viana], Enzo, Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] and everyone at City who has made this deal possible. I want to take the faith shown in me and repay it as soon as possible.”

Fernandez a “complete midfielder”

The fee City have paid for Fernandez is obviously reflective of how highly they think of the Argentina international.

Fernandez scored 31 goals and provided 29 assists after joining Chelsea from Benfica in 2023, and sporting director Hugo Viana was effusive in his praise of what he brings to the table.

“At Manchester City, we are always looking to bring in world-class players and Enzo fits the bill,” Viana said.

“He is a complete midfielder: technically gifted, hardworking, tenacious and a goalscorer.

“He is adept at playing different styles of football. He is comfortable playing a possession-based game, and he can play on the counter effectively, too.

“To have played in two World Cup finals and won major trophies in multiple countries at just 25 says everything you need to know about his mentality, professionalism and technical quality.

“We are delighted to bring him here and feel very strongly he will improve our team.”

articles.summary: Mudryk worked with De Zerbi at Shakhtar.
articles.content:
Murdyk excited for De Zerbi reunion after Tottenham seal loan deal for Chelsea winger

Mudryk worked with De Zerbi at Shakhtar.

Last Update:

Mykhailo Mudryk expressed his delight at reuniting with Roberto De Zerbi after Tottenham sealed a loan deal for the Chelsea winger.

The Ukrainian has not played competitive football since November 2024, having resolved a doping case with the Football Association last month.

Mudryk joined Chelsea in 2023 having made his breakthrough at Shakhtar Donetsk in 2021-22 under De Zerbi.

And, after completing a deal that features a £75m option to make the transfer permanent, Mudryk is relishing the opportunity to play for the Italian again.

“It’s a great feeling. I can’t wait to start training and playing for the club, and I’m so excited to be reunited with Roberto De Zerbi,” Mudryk told Tottenham’s official website.

“I’m a player who brings speed and creativity, and I want to help in both the offensive and defensive areas. I want to make the fans excited.

“I can see it’s a strong squad here with good players, and I’m looking forward to sharing a pitch and special moments with them.”

Tottenham turned to Mudryk after a deal for Everton winger Iliman Ndiaye broke down. Ndiaye has since signed for Manchester City.

But De Zerbi has hope he can get the best out of a player he believes to be a game-changer.

“Having worked with Misha earlier in his career, I know exactly what he can bring to our team,” De Zerbi said.

“He has the quality to change a game with his speed and ability in one-vs-one situations, and is an exciting, attacking talent.

“I will demand a lot from Misha and it is our job to help him find the best version of himself. If we do that then he can become a very important player for us. I am very happy he chose to come here, and I cannot wait to work with him again.”

Tottenham are also set to sign defender Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea on a permanent deal, having allowed Kevin Danso to join Sunderland on loan with an obligation to buy that is contingent on the Black Cats staying in the Premier League.

Despite spending over £300m in the transfer window, Tottenham suffered defeat in each of their opening two Premier League games. They sit joint-bottom of the table at this very early stage of the season. Spurs visit Nottingham Forest on Saturday, when Mudryk could make his debut.

Chelsea agree Camara deal following Fernandez departure

Last Update:

Chelsea have agreed a deal in principle to sign Senegal midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco following the departure of Enzo Fernandez.

The Blues earlier on deadline day agreed to part with Argentina international Fernandez, who is set to complete a move to Manchester City for a British record-tying fee of £125million.

It had been though that Chelsea would be unable to source a replacement, with Monaco reported to have rejected two offers for Camara and Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini said to have blocked France international Manu Kone from leaving the Stadio Olimpico.

But, with under two hours left in the transfer window, Fabrizio Romano reported Chelsea have come to terms on a €55million (£47m) deal for Camara, who has been given permission to undergo a medical.

Camara will reportedly sign a contract until 2032 with the option for an additional year.

The 22-year-old has made 73 appearances, with 66 starts, for Monaco since joining from Metz in 2024.

He has won 49 caps for Senegal, scoring seven goals, and played in all four of the Lions of Teranga’s games at the 2026 World Cup as they exited the tournament in the round of 32.
