Alonso made decision to leave Fernandez out of Chelsea win

Argentina midfielder has been linked with a move to Manchester City

Last Update:

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said he left Enzo Fernandez out of the squad to face Luton because he had to do ‘what is best for the team.’

Alonso said in the build-up to the Carabao Cup tie that he expected Fernandez to play.

Chelsea had set a deadline of last Friday for Manchester City to sign the Argentina international. However, they are still said to be open to a sale if they get at least £120million and are able to sign a replacement.

But the midfielder was surprisingly not involved as Alonso fielded a strong team against League One opposition.

Alonso said: “We assess individually, collectively, what is the best for the team. We made that decision.

“It was our decision from myself and the club. It’s just because of the game today and we needed players to get minutes.”

Fernandez was a second-half substitute as Alonso’s men began their Premier League campaign with a 3-2 win over west London rivals Fulham on Monday.

Alonso would not be drawn but did drop Robert Sanchez for the cup tie with Mike Penders making his debut.

Alonso said: “I like to talk about the players in my changing room. It’s not respectful to speak on other things.

“We are happy with the squad we have. I have always said that we need to be aware of situations. In this period, we can make decisions. Let’s see what happens.”

articles.title: Derek McInnes ’embarrassed’ as Rangers suffer shock Conference League exit
articles.summary: Rangers' poor start to the season continues
articles.content:
Derek McInnes ’embarrassed’ as Rangers suffer shock Conference League exit

Rangers' poor start to the season continues

Last Update:

Rangers manager Derek McInnes said he takes “full responsibility” after his side crashed out of Europe on Thursday night.

Holding a 1-0 aggregate lead heading into the second leg of their UEFA Conference League play-off against Jablonec in the Czech Republic, the Scottish outfit were beaten 4-3 on penalties following a grueling 120-minute contest. Despite leading early in the shootout, spot-kick misses from Findlay Curtis and James Penrice sealed their elimination.

The result leaves Rangers without European football beyond August for the first time since their 2017 defeat to Progrès Niederkörn, ramping up early pressure on McInnes following a difficult start to his Ibrox tenure.

Speaking after a match in which Rangers registered just one shot on target and under 47% possession, McInnes pulled no punches regarding the display.

“I’m embarrassed with the performance,” the Rangers manager said.

“The only people who represented the club well tonight were my staff and the supporters who were outstanding, getting behind the team despite watching what we all watched.

“I’m not going to make any excuses. Yes there’s been a big turnover of players, yes we looked inexperienced at times but the responsibility is mine to make sure we’re better than what we served up tonight.

“We got what we deserved. If we’d won on penalties we would have taken it, of course, but it would only have covered over the cracks.

“I’m mortified with the performance. I know you can lose games of football but we should have enough in the building to take care of that tonight.”

Rangers, who have one point from two games in the Premiership so far, face Aberdeen on Sunday.

articles.title: UEFA announces it will ensure ‘credible’ Infantino alternative as it officially withdraws FIFA competition boycott
articles.summary: UEFA will allow its member nations to compete in FIFA competitions but insisted trust in Gianni Infantino is broken beyond repair.
articles.content:
UEFA announces it will ensure ‘credible’ Infantino alternative as it officially withdraws FIFA competition boycott

UEFA will allow its member nations to compete in FIFA competitions but insisted trust in Gianni Infantino is broken beyond repair.

Last Update:

UEFA has provisionally ended plans to boycott FIFA competitions in response to Gianni Infantino‘s failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, but will work to ensure a “credible alternative” should he seek re-election as FIFA president.

News emerged on Thursday that UEFA had applied for the release of documents related to the conception of the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan as it seeks to take criminal legal action against Infantino in Switzerland.

Infantino’s planned scheme sparked outrage across the football world, with UEFA, European football’s governing body, threatening to withdraw its teams from FIFA competitions.

Having received assurances that the FFE plan will not be revived, UEFA will allow its member nations to compete in FIFA competitions in the coming season.

However, following a meeting in Monaco ahead of the draws for this season’s European club competitions, UEFA made it clear that the withdrawal of the FFE proposals could not restore the loss of trust in Infantino.

In a statement, UEFA said its president Aleksander Ceferin and its administration had been unanimously mandated to “pursue every available institutional, political and legal avenue necessary to secure fundamental reform, restore proper limits on presidential authority and ensure that FIFA is once again governed as an institution”.

UEFA said the first step must be an independent external review of the FFE plan, with “full access to all relevant documents and communications”.

Infantino is scheduled to run unopposed next March as he seeks re-election as president.

However, should he indeed seek a term another term, UEFA said it would “join forces with its partner confederations to ensure that Member Associations are offered a credible alternative – one committed to integrity, accountability, development and genuine institutional change”.

Infantino has served as FIFA president since 2016, taking over after predecessor Sepp Blatter resigned in 2015 amid a corruption probe and was subsequently banned for eight years by the body’s ethics committee.

UEFA statement in full

Shortly after news of its plan to pursue criminal proceedings against Infantino emerged, UEFA released a lengthy statement, which read:

“Meeting in Monaco on the occasion of the 2026/27 UEFA club competition draws, National Association representatives serving on the UEFA Executive Committee and European FIFA Council members were joined by the Presidents of European National Associations present in Monaco to discuss the continuing crisis at FIFA.

“The meeting reviewed the fallout from the FIFA President’s aborted attempt to sell an interest in the FIFA World Cup to outside investors – a scheme which exposed a profound failure of judgement, an abuse of presidential power and a conception of leadership incompatible with the duties of the highest office in world football.

“Those present unanimously mandated the UEFA President and Administration to pursue every available institutional, political and legal avenue necessary to secure fundamental reform, restore proper limits on presidential authority and ensure that FIFA is once again governed as an institution – not around one individual.

“The first step must be a genuinely independent external review of FIFA Forward Enterprise, with full access to all relevant documents, communications and decision-making records.  FIFA cannot investigate itself and expect the football community simply to accept its conclusions.

“But the consequences of this crisis go beyond governance.  The trust required to exercise the office of FIFA President has been broken and cannot be restored by withdrawing one proposal, issuing assurances or promising reform after the event.  World football now needs new leadership capable of rebuilding that trust.

“UEFA will therefore continue working with Confederations, Member Associations and the wider football community – including fans, players, clubs, leagues and others – to shape the future of FIFA.  Should the current FIFA President nevertheless seek another mandate, UEFA will join forces with its partner confederations to ensure that Member Associations are offered a credible alternative – one committed to integrity, accountability, development and genuine institutional change.”

The statement continued by questioning why Infantino felt the need to secure outside investment when FIFA reportedly had reserves of $2.7billion at the end of 2025. It also confirmed that plans for a FIFA competition boycott had been shelved following guarantees there would be no revival of the FFE proposals.

“FIFA has currently billions of dollars in reserves,” it continued. This money belongs to the Member Associations.

“Together with other Confederations, UEFA will jointly explore a responsible release of part of FIFA’s reserves for the benefit of the Member Associations – while at the same time ensuring that any proposal preserves FIFA’s financial stability. The question is therefore why the FIFA President believed he needed outside investors to expand development funding.

“The delegates were also informed that FIFA has now confirmed in writing to UEFA that the FIFA Forward Enterprise project has been “irrevocably and permanently withdrawn” and that it “will not re-appear in any other shape, construction, name or form”.

“Having now secured the two assurances it required from FIFA on 30 July, and following consultation with its National Associations, UEFA has therefore agreed to suspend, on a provisional basis, the withdrawal by European teams from FIFA competitions in the coming season, including the Women’s U20 World Cup, U17 World Cup and the Women’s U17 World Cup.  This position will remain under constant review and may be reconsidered immediately if circumstances so require.

“While the immediate question of participation has now been resolved, the underlying crisis has not.

“The abandonment of FFE does not erase the deception, intimidation and abuse of power that made it possible.  Nor does it restore the confidence that has been lost.

“This is not a choice between good governance and football development. Nor is this about Europe seeking greater power within FIFA.  It is simply about ensuring that no part of world football – large or small, those with more and those with less – is dependent on the power of one individual.

“FIFA has a fundamental responsibility to support every Member Association and this responsibility must be strengthened, not weakened.  But development is an institutional obligation – not a presidential favour – and no Member Association should ever have to choose between the resources to which it is entitled and the freedom to exercise its own judgement.

“UEFA’s position remains unequivocal: whether it is the World Cup or an Under-15 tournament, FIFA’s competitions are not for sale.  Neither is the governance of our game.  FIFA’s development resources must likewise never become instruments of personal or political influence.  They belong to world football and must be protected by transparent, objective rules.

“FIFA must once again be governed as an institution serving football – not operate as an instrument of individual power.”

FIFA has not responded to a request for comment regarding UEFA’s plans for criminal action against Infantino.

articles.title: Champions League: Arsenal to face Real Madrid and Bayern Munich
articles.summary: See the full list of group fixtures
articles.content:
Champions League: Arsenal to face Real Madrid and Bayern Munich

See the full list of group fixtures

Last Update:

Last year’s runners-up Arsenal will take on Real Madrid and Bayern Munich in the Champions League group phase, while holders PSG play both Manchester City and Aston Villa.

Liverpool take on Inter Milan and Atletico Madrid, Manchester City play Barcelona, Manchester United have a tricky run of games including Bayern Munich and Roma, while Aston Villa have some blockbuster fixtures.

The Champions League continues with its league-phase format, meaning there are no traditional groups of four. Instead, each of the 36 clubs will play eight matches against eight different opponents, with four games at home and four away.

See the full fixtures here.

Table of Contents

Who the seeds will play

Who the Premier League sides play

Champions League – Full list of qualified teams

Champions League format

In a change from the group stage format conducted until 2023/24, each team now plays eight matches in the league phase, all against different opponents.

Four of those matches will be at home and four away, with the opponents determined according to four seeding pots split by rankings.

Teams will play two opponents from each of those pots – one against a team from each pot at home and one away. The results decide the overall standings in one league.

The top eight sides in the table qualify automatically for the round of 16. The teams finishing in ninth to 24th will compete in a two-legged knockout phase play-off to reach the last 16.

Teams finishing 25th or lower are out of Europe for the season.

English teams in the Champions League: Why are there five clubs?

Arsenal, City, United, Villa and Liverpool.qualified as the top five teams in the Premier League.

England was awarded extra positions as a result of UEFA’s co-efficient rankings, which are based on the overall performances of nations across European competition over a season.

Villa also won last season’s Europa League, which would have earned the Villans a place in the Champions League had they not qualified through their league position.

When is the Champions League final?

The final will take place on June 5 2027 at the Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid, which has been Atletico Madrid’s home since 2017.

That could be a good omen for English teams: two Premier League sides reached the final when Atleti’s home previously hosted the showpiece in 2019, Liverpool beating Tottenham 2-0.

articles.title: UEFA pursuing criminal complaint against Infantino over failed World Cup sell-off plan
articles.summary: UEFA is set to pursue action against Infantino in Switzerland.
articles.content:
UEFA pursuing criminal complaint against Infantino over failed World Cup sell-off plan

UEFA is set to pursue action against Infantino in Switzerland.

Last Update:

UEFA is preparing to bring criminal claims against FIFA president Gianni Infantino over his failed proposals to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino’s FIFA Forward Enterprise Plan sparked outrage across the football world, with UEFA threatening to boycott the World Cup in response.

With the plans having since been dropped, that threat has now been withdrawn, but European football’s governing body has made it clear it has no confidence of Infantino’s leadership of FIFA. Infantino is up for re-election next March and is currently due to run unopposed.

And, in the latest development in the fallout from Infantino’s proposals, UEFA has applied for the release of documents related to the their conception as it seeks to take criminal legal action against him in Switzerland.

UEFA has made an application in the United States for information from world football’s governing body and from Thrive Capital, the investment firm founded by Joshua Kushner, the younger brother of US president Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner.

As part of the plans, Thrive and Kushner were set to serve as anchor investors and pay $4.2billion to FIFA  for a 20 per cent share of the FIFA Forward Enterprise subsidiary that would run the World Cup and other major FIFA events.

UEFA’s application states: “On July 28, 2026, without consulting the FIFA Council, UEFA, or any of the other confederations, or any of the 211 FIFA member associations, Infantino, purportedly acting on behalf of FIFA, publicly announced a plan to place the commercial rights to the men’s and women’s World Cups and the Club World Cup into a new subsidiary: FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

“That announcement by Infantino was the public unveiling of a plan that he and a small circle of co-conspirators had conceived and reportedly been developing in secret for more than a year.

“UEFA and other interested parties are preparing to bring criminal claims in Switzerland against Infantino and possibly other FIFA officials and advisors for criminal mismanagement.

“The secretive structuring, valuation, financing, and marketing inflicted direct and concrete injury on FIFA’s reputation, governance authority, and commercial relationships to the detriment of FIFA as well as its 211 members, including UEFA’s 55 member associations.”

UEFA alleges that the plan was designed by Infantino to enrich himself and potential investors.

“In truth, it was a vehicle for Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from FIFA’s most valuable assets to the detriment of FIFA, its members, and other parties within the football family,” the application states.

“Infantino pushed the plan through internal FIFA approval only days earlier at a hastily convened meeting where a limited number of FIFA’s management officials and employees – some of whom had never heard of the plan – were given mere hours to sign off on an unprecedented multi-billion dollar scheme.”

UEFA also took issue with the valuation of the stakes on offer. It claims the valuations were not independently verified and that the stakes would have been available at too cheap of a price.

The application adds: “Under the terms Infantino announced, those investors stood to acquire a permanent financial interest in FIFA’s commercial arm for $4.2bn, implying an absurdly low enterprise value of only approximately $20bn, a figure that was neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer.

“The valuation work exchanged with Thrive, and any internal Thrive analyses of FIFA’s enterprise value, are directly probative of whether the $4.2bn price reflected an arm’s-length valuation of FIFA’s commercial rights or, as the public record indicates, a fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit.”

FIFA and UEFA have been contacted for comment.

Villa continue overhaul with Goretzka signing

Former Bayern man brings bags of experience

Last Update:

Aston Villa have signed former Bayern Munich midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free transfer.

The 31-year-old left Bayern at the end of last season having won seven Bundesliga titles and the Champions League.

He offers much-needed class and experience to a Villa side in the midst of a complete overhaul as Unai Emery prepares for a Champions League campaign.

Villa have been looking to add to a midfield that has lost the services of Youri Tielemans, who left for Manchester United, with Amadou Onana out of action after rupturing his ACL while playing for Belgium at the World Cup.

The former Schalke midfielder made 48 appearances for Bayern last season, scoring five goals, all of which came in the Bundesliga.

In his time eight seasons at Bayern, Goretzka made 312 appearances, scoring 51 goals. He won seven Bundesliga titles, three DFB-Pokals and one Champions League title.

articles.title: Iraola refuses to rule out Gakpo departure as Barcola deal close to completion
articles.summary: Cody Gakpo could be on his way out of Liverpool before the transfer window closes.
articles.content:
Iraola refuses to rule out Gakpo departure as Barcola deal close to completion

Cody Gakpo could be on his way out of Liverpool before the transfer window closes.

Last Update:

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has refused to guarantee that Cody Gakpo will remain at Anfield amid continued interest from Tottenham and Manchester City.

There have not yet been any direct talks between Liverpool and either club over a potential deal for Gakpo, but both sides have been monitoring the Netherlands international’s situation.

Gakpo’s future could be affected by Liverpool’s expected arrival of Paris Saint-Germain forward Bradley Barcola, with the France international having been the club’s priority target throughout the summer.

Liverpool have now agreed a deal worth around £120m to sign Barcola, although the transfer is yet to be completed.

Speaking at his news conference on Thursday, Iraola confirmed Liverpool are looking to strengthen their options on the wings.

“As you know we are trying to sign in that position [wingers] and we cannot talk about players that right now are not ours but it is evident we are trying to improve and fill or trying to fill that position because we don’t have the numbers,” Iraola said.

“I hope we can have good news soon but we are still not there.”

Gakpo praised despite uncertain future

Gakpo scored in Liverpool’s 2-2 Premier League draw with Newcaste on Sunday and has shown no signs of pushing for a move away from the club.

However, Barcola predominantly operates from the left wing, which could leave Gakpo facing increased competition for minutes if the transfer is completed.

The 27-year-old could therefore consider his options if he feels his chances of regular first-team football will be reduced.

Iraola was full of praise for Gakpo’s performances but admitted there could be no guarantees while the transfer window remains open.

“I can say what I said last week, and even after the performance he had in the first game,” he said.

“He is playing very well for us, he has been very good since he came back from the World Cup and after the holidays, a good attitude and I hope we can keep him at that level because he has been very influential.

“When the market is open you cannot guarantee anything with anyone.

“When I arrived I would like to know how the market finishes and then when you finish with this one and this one but I don’t know what is going to happen with any of our players. I cannot guarantee anything.

“You think I can smell who we are going to sign or what position but experience shows you that, if there is an opportunity on the last day, let’s take it.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Tottenham sign Omar Marmoush from Manchester City
articles.summary: Tottenham have announced the signing of Omar Marmoush from Manchester City.
articles.content:
BREAKING: Tottenham sign Omar Marmoush from Manchester City

Tottenham have announced the signing of Omar Marmoush from Manchester City.

Last Update:

Tottenham have announced the signing of Egypt international forward Omar Marmoush from Manchester City on a season-long loan.

The deal includes an obligation for Spurs to make the move permanent next summer, with Marmoush becoming the latest addition to Roberto De Zerbi’s squad.

Marmoush said he was excited to join Tottenham and believes the club’s project was a major factor in his decision.

“It feels amazing to be here. I’m so excited to get started with the team and I can’t wait to meet the fans,” he said.

“Tottenham Hotspur is one of the biggest clubs in England, if not the world, and the project was very attractive to me.

“I’ve spoken with the Head Coach, I loved what he had to say and I’m sure our passion for the game will go very well together.”

Tottenham sporting director Johan Lange described Marmoush’s arrival as a statement of the club’s ambition.

“Omar is a quality player and his arrival represents a statement of our intent,” Lange said.

“He has demonstrated that he can perform at the highest level, and we believe he can play a major role in what we want to achieve over the coming years.”

Table of Contents

De Zerbi welcomes eighth signing

De Zerbi also welcomed the Egypt international, highlighting his attacking ability and desire to improve.

“Omar is exactly the kind of player we want at this club – ambitious, hungry and determined to make a difference,” he said.

“He has incredible attacking quality but what I also love is his desire to improve and to win.

“He brings pace, intelligence and a real threat in front of goal, and I believe he can take our attacking play to another level.”

Marmoush began his professional career with Wadi Degla in Egypt, making his debut at the age of 17 in July 2016 before moving to Germany to join Wolfsburg the following year.

After initially playing for Wolfsburg’s youth side, he made his senior debut in May 2020 and subsequently spent time on loan at St Pauli and Stuttgart.

His breakthrough came during his loan spell with Stuttgart in the 2021-22 season, when he scored on his debut and won the Bundesliga Rookie of the Month award twice.

Marmoush returned to Wolfsburg for the 2022-23 campaign and made 48 appearances, scoring six goals, before joining Eintracht Frankfurt in May 2023.

He scored 17 goals in 41 appearances during his first season at Frankfurt and continued to impress the following campaign, winning the Bundesliga Player of the Month award in September and November 2024.

Marmoush finished his Frankfurt career with 37 goals and 20 assists in 67 appearances before joining Manchester City in January 2025.

Immediate impact in England

He made an immediate impact in England, scoring a hat-trick in a 4-0 win over Newcastle United in February 2025.

Marmoush made 25 appearances in his first half-season at City, scoring eight goals, before claiming the Premier League Goal of the Season award for his strike against Bournemouth in May 2025.

He ended his City spell with 16 goals in 62 appearances and helped the club win the Carabao Cup and FA Cup.

At international level, Marmoush scored on his Egypt debut against Libya in October 2021 and has since won 55 caps and scored 11 goals.

He helped Egypt reach the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations final, has featured at three Africa Cup of Nations tournaments and represented his country at his first World Cup this summer.

articles.title: Jaissle hails Gonzalez addition but will ‘push every day’ for more Newcastle signings
articles.summary: Newcastle's manager is keen to add further to his squad before the deadline.
articles.content:
Jaissle hails Gonzalez addition but will ‘push every day’ for more Newcastle signings

Newcastle's manager is keen to add further to his squad before the deadline.

Last Update:

Matthias Jaissle will “push every day” for Newcastle United to make more signings after hailing the addition of Nico Gonzalez.

Gonzalez was unveiled as Newcastle’s seventh signing of the transfer window, and the second since Jaissle was officially confirmed as former manager Eddie Howe’s successor, ahead of their EFL Cup tie with West Brom on Wednesday.

Newcastle claimed a 3-2 win over the early Championship pace-setters thanks to a debut goal from Bazoumana Toure and a double from substitute Harvey Barnes.

The arrival of Gonzalez from Premier League rivals Manchester City in a £52million deal stands as the most important signing of the summer for Newcastle, with the former Barcelona and Porto man set to slot as the number six and become the leader of a midfield that has lost Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali this summer.

But with Newcastle reportedly looking to make additions further forward in the final days of the transfer window, Jaissle made it clear he is not fully satisfied with his squad as it stands.

“I will push every day,” Jaissle said when asked about the need for new signings in his post-match press conference.

Gonzalez made 59 appearances for City and, at the age of 24, has significant experience of Premier League and European football.

And Jaissle believes his combination of youth and experience makes Gonzalez an ideal fit for Newcastle, who earlier explored moves for older players in the form of Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg and Joao Palhinha.

“We’re really happy to have him now finally here,” Jaissle added. “It was a long fight. I’m really happy because we continue our brave way with young lads, with talented players. Nico is young but also experienced, so I think this is a perfect fit and combination.

“He brings a lot of quality into the squad. This is very important, so we can’t wait to see him on the pitch. I’m really much looking forward to it.

“We want to continue our brave way, not bringing in some guys who are almost retired. We want to continue our approach, so we are bringing a young lad in with Nico, but already an experienced one in the Premier League, many, many matches on his statistics.

“He brings a lot of quality in possession, but also physically wise he’s also able to bring impact out of possession, so I think it’s a great addition to our squad.”

In terms of outgoings, Joe Willock has been linked with a move to Besiktas while there is talk of forward Nick Woltemade being loaned out a year after signing in a club-record deal.

Jaissle expects both to remain beyond the end of the window, though he left the door open when asked about potential departures.

“For all the players I expect them to stay,” Jaissle said. “But you know as well football is quite complex and things can change from one day to the other.”

articles.title: Maresca keen to add a ‘captain’ at Manchester City before transfer window shuts
articles.summary: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says his side are not done in the transfer window.
articles.content:
Maresca keen to add a ‘captain’ at Manchester City before transfer window shuts

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says his side are not done in the transfer window.

Last Update:

Enzo Maresca has hinted that Manchester City could make further additions before the transfer window closes, with the manager hoping to bring another experienced leader into his squad.

City have lost a significant amount of experience this summer, with Bernardo Silva, John Stones, Nathan Ake and Rodri all departing.

Maresca fielded City’s youngest opening-day XI since 2008 in their 2-1 win over Bournemouth on Sunday, and the Italian believes the squad would benefit from adding more senior figures.

Reports claim that City are expected to make an offer for Enzo Fernandez, who captained Chelsea last season, before the transfer deadline on 1 September.

“We have experienced players,” Maresca said.

“For sure, we have leaders. Now we need to wait four or five more days when the transfer window closes if we can add one or two more captains to Ruben [Dias] and Erling [Haaland], who at the moment are the two captains.

“It’s the transfer window. Anything can happen. We’ll see. It’s four or five more days to go.”

Busy few days ahead at City

City are also set to welcome Ayyoub Bouaddi into the squad for Friday’s trip to Crystal Palace after the midfielder completed his €100m move from Lille on Wednesday.

Elliot Anderson is available to travel after recovering from the cramp that forced him off against Bournemouth.

Meanwhile, Omar Marmoush is close to completing his move to Tottenham, while Jack Grealish remains the subject of transfer interest from Sunderland.

Grealish came off the bench against Bournemouth but his future remains uncertain.

“Jack is here until the day that he’s here,” Maresca said.

“It’s my duty to try to help him to give us the best and then we’ll see in the next four or five days what happens. I speak with Jack almost every day.”

articles.title: Atletico board unanimously approves decision not to sell Alvarez to Barcelona
articles.summary: The club is united behind the decision.
articles.content:
Atletico board unanimously approves decision not to sell Alvarez to Barcelona

The club is united behind the decision.

Last Update:

Atletico Madrid‘s board has given its unanimous support to the decision not to negotiate a sale of Julian Alvarez to Barcelona.

Alvarez is under contract at the Metropolitano until 2030 but has stated his desire to fulfil his “dream” by moving to Camp Nou.

The Argentina forward was booed and walked straight down the tunnel at full-time of Atletico’s LaLiga opener, a 2-2 draw with Villarreal, having come on as a second-half substitute.

Alvarez missed training on Wednesday, reportedly due to illness, as Atletico hit back at comments from Joan Laporta, with the Barca president saying the club retained an interest in the former Manchester City star because of the suggestion the Rojiblancos would be willing to sell to Arsenal.

In response, Atletico said there was a “0% chance” of Alvarez being sold to Barca.

And in a statement released on Thursday, the club announced its board is fully behind that stance.

It read: “The members of Atlético de Madrid’s Board of Directors have unanimously expressed their absolute support for the club’s decision to not negotiate the transfer of Julián Alvarez to FC Barcelona.

“The members of the Board of Directors acknowledge that “Atlético de Madrid is open to standard transfer market negotiations when conducted in a professional, ethical and respectful manner. We fully stand behind the club’s previously communicated position that FC Barcelona failed to meet these requirements and, as a result, there will not be any negotiation and there is zero consideration of an Alvarez transfer to Barcelona.”

“Atlético de Madrid trust that our player will understand the decision and will remain focused on helping the club achieve its goals, just as he has done during the two seasons he has been defending our colours.”

articles.title: Delap backs Glasner to help him ‘make the next step’ after completing £50m Forest move
articles.summary: Forest have paid a club-record fee for Delap.
articles.content:
Delap backs Glasner to help him ‘make the next step’ after completing £50m Forest move

Forest have paid a club-record fee for Delap.

Last Update:

Nottingham Forest have completed the signing of Liam Delap from Chelsea on a five-year deal, with the striker convinced boss Oliver Glasner can take his career to the next level.

Forest are reported to have paid a club-record £50million to take Delap to the City Ground.

Delap joined Chelsea from Ipswich Town in June last year, but he made a minimal impact in his only season at Stamford Bridge.

Though he won the Club World Cup soon after joining the club, Delap scored just three goals in 47 appearances for the Blues.

Glasner key to Delap’s Forest move

Delap netted 12 goals for Ipswich in 2024-25 in a campaign that saw them relegated from the Premier League, and is hopeful he can recapture that kind of form under Glasner at Forest.

“I really can’t wait to get started, this is a massive club with a big history,” Delap told Forest’s official website.

“I spoke to the manager and I like his way, I think he can be the one to really help me develop and make that next step and hopefully I can bring goals here.

“I can’t wait to hear the noise at the City Ground and have the fans on my side because I know how loud and important they are.

“As a team we can build something really strong and the main aim is to challenge and be a top club in the Premier League.”

Forest lost their opening two games of the season, suffering a 1-0 defeat to Leeds United at the City Ground in their Premier League opener before the same opposition beat them 2-0 in the EFL Cup on Tuesday.

Delap could make his debut for Forest when they visit Liverpool on Saturday.

articles.title: De Zerbi reveals Savio goals target after ‘perfect’ Tottenham debut
articles.summary: Savio got off the mark in a hurry following his move from Man City.
articles.content:
De Zerbi reveals Savio goals target after ‘perfect’ Tottenham debut

Savio got off the mark in a hurry following his move from Man City.

Last Update:

Roberto De Zerbi revealed he has set new Tottenham signing Savio a target of scoring 10 to 12 goals after he opened his account on what was described as a “perfect” debut by the Spurs boss.

Named on the bench after completing his move from Manchester City for an initial £75m, Savio came on in the second half of Tottenham’s EFL Cup second-round tie with Charlton Athletic and had a swift impact as Spurs prevailed 5-1. They will face Liverpool at Anfield in the third round.

Savio cut in from the right to fire home his first Tottenham goal from the edge of the area to make it 4-1. He then appeared to have a second, but the goal was credited to team-mate Ben Davies after his strike deflected off the full-back’s hip.

De Zerbi sets ambitious Savio target

The size of the fee for Savio raised eyebrows given his relatively limited impact in two seasons at City.

He scored just seven goals in his time at the Etihad Stadium and has only once hit double digits in his career, doing so while on loan at Girona in 2023-24, when he found the net 11 times.

But De Zerbi is hoping Savio can prove a prolific presence for Tottenham after quickly getting off the mark.

“It was a perfect day for him,” De Zerbi said. “I think his biggest step and biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals.

“With his qualities, he is one of the best wingers. But the best wingers score many goals.

“I spoke with him yesterday, two days ago. We put the goal on 10 to 12 goals because we need those goals from the wingers.

“Last season, I think we suffered too much. Also, because the number of goals were not enough to compete for nothing more than that position.”

Savio could make his Premier League debut for Tottenham on Saturday when they host Newcastle United.

articles.title: Mourinho: Mbappe ‘hungry’ to make history as Real Madrid hit form
articles.summary: Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho was full of praise for Kylian Mbappe following his recent hat-trick.
articles.content:
Mourinho: Mbappe ‘hungry’ to make history as Real Madrid hit form

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho was full of praise for Kylian Mbappe following his recent hat-trick.

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho believes Kylian Mbappe is “hungry to make history” at Real Madrid after the forward scored a hat-trick in their 4-1 LaLiga win over Real Sociedad on Wednesday.

Mbappe opened the scoring before Luka Sucic equalised shortly after, leaving the sides level at half-time in Real Madrid’s first home game of the season.

The France international then struck twice more after the break, while Vinicius Junior also found the net as Real Madrid secured a second successive victory under Mourinho.

“This guy [Mbappe] is incredible,” Mourinho said after the game.

“I’m happy that he made history at the World Cup because there were 25 world champion players, but only one is for eternity in football, the player with most goals at a World Cup.

“He looks hungry to make history with Real Madrid.”

Mbappe did not score in Real Madrid’s 2-1 win over Espanyol on the opening weekend, although he played a part in setting up Carlos Espi’s late winner.

Mourinho was asked how many goals he expects Mbappe to score this season, particularly given that Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo both scored more than 45 LaLiga goals in a single season during his previous spell in charge of Real Madrid.

“If it’s 60, 40, 50? I can’t say,” Mourinho said. “I’d prefer 40 goals but with trophies, or 40 goals with a lot of work.

“I’m very happy with him, technically there’s nothing to say obviously, but in the group, he’s taking responsibility, he got back two days early from his holiday.

“Today I left him on the field for 90 minutes, I thought he might score four.”

Mourinho happy with second-half response

The result also marked an encouraging return to the Bernabeu for Mourinho, although the home supporters expressed their frustration during a first half in which Real Sociedad competed strongly.

“We know the Bernabeu, the players know it, I know it,” Mourinho said.

“Thankfully they’re like that, because it’s a consequence of history.

“Real Madrid always have great teams and players, and the fans want more. They pay to have their emotions, their happiness, their frustration.”

Mourinho was ultimately pleased with the response from his players and believes Real Madrid will regularly produce high-scoring performances.

“In the end we got what we wanted, the three points, and the fans went home with a taste of what we can do,” he added.

“Scoring three, four, five [goals], we’ll do that a lot.”

Real Sociedad manager Pellegrino Matarazzo felt his side could take encouragement from their performance despite suffering their second defeat of the season.

“Today we showed that at the Bernabeu, in the first 45 to 60 minutes, we were able to compete against a world-class team,” Matarazzo said.

“The players are gaining experience, players who are new to the team. So there are a lot of positives that we take away.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Liverpool strike agreement to sign Bradley Barcola from PSG
articles.summary: Bradley Barcola looks set to join Liverpool this summer.
articles.content:
BREAKING: Liverpool strike agreement to sign Bradley Barcola from PSG

Bradley Barcola looks set to join Liverpool this summer.

Last Update:

Liverpool have reached an agreement in principle with Paris Saint-Germain to sign forward Bradley Barcola in a deal worth around £120m, according to The Athletic.

More than £100m of the package is guaranteed, with the two clubs agreeing the broad terms of the transfer overnight.

Liverpool sporting director Richard Hughes and Fenway Sports Group president Mike Gordon are overseeing the negotiations, with the final details now being worked through.

The move could also have consequences for Cody Gakpo, who has been linked with Tottenham throughout the summer and has also attracted interest from Manchester City.

Liverpool identified Barcola as their leading target to replace Mohamed Salah earlier in the summer, with the club preparing an opening offer for the France international in July.

Salah replacement

The 23-year-old has two years remaining on his PSG contract but has made it clear that he does not intend to extend his stay with the European champions.

He was subsequently left out of PSG’s squad for their Ligue 1 opener against Rennes, which ended in a 2-2 draw.

Barcola predominantly operates on the left wing but can also play on the opposite flank. He faced competition for places from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue last season and was often used from the bench during the latter stages of PSG’s Champions League campaign.

Despite that competition, Barcola made 49 appearances in all competitions during the 2025-26 season, scoring 13 goals and providing seven assists as PSG retained the Ligue 1 title and continued their success in Europe.

Since breaking into the first team, the Lyon academy product has registered 39 goals and 37 assists in 152 appearances for the club.

Barcola also played a major role for France at this summer’s World Cup, featuring in all eight matches and scoring three goals.

articles.title: Villa agree Jackson deal as Watkins closes in on Al Hilal move
articles.summary: Unai Emery will have a new striker leading the line.
articles.content:
Villa agree Jackson deal as Watkins closes in on Al Hilal move

Unai Emery will have a new striker leading the line.

Last Update:

Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sign striker Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea, who is set to replace Ollie Watkins as he heads to Al Hilal.

According to The Athletic’s David Ornstein, Villa have agreed a deal worth up to £65million with Chelsea for Jackson. They will pay an initial £47.5million, with the rest of the package made up by £17.5m in add-ons.

Jackson is set to fill the void by Watkins, for whom Al Hilal are finalising a £50m deal with Villa.

Watkins will become the latest key member of the Villa side that won the Europa League and finished fourth last season to depart the club.

Villa have also seen Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne leave in what has been a difficult summer for Unai Emery’s side.

In Watkins, they will be losing a player who has scored 108 goals in 278 games since joining from Brentford in 2020.

Watkins was not in the squad for Villa’s dreadful 4-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion in their Premier League opener, with Emery cutting a very frustrated figure as he neglected to explain his absence.

The 30-year-old later apologised and returned to training, but it is clear he has now played his last game for the club.

Jackson was surplus to requirements at Chelsea, having spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich.

The Senegal international scored 11 goals in 34 games for Bayern, where he won the Bundesliga title and DFB-Pokal. He had previously scored 30 goals in 81 appearances for Chelsea, with Jackson proving too inconsistent in front of goal to be trusted to lead the line for the Blues.

With Emery having a reputation for getting the best out of players, he will hope to succeed where Chelsea failed in helping Jackson find that consistency. In Watkins, Jackson has a tough act to follow and, if the transfer is finalised in time, he could make his debut against champions Arsenal on Monday.

articles.title: EFL Cup round-up: Newcastle beat West Brom in thriller, Barry hat-trick sends Everton through
articles.summary: The Magpies were forced to survive a scare.
articles.content:
EFL Cup round-up: Newcastle beat West Brom in thriller, Barry hat-trick sends Everton through

The Magpies were forced to survive a scare.

Last Update:

Newcastle United claimed their first win under Matthias Jaissle as they edged a spirted West Brom 3-2 in the second round of the EFL Cup.

The Magpies produced an impressive performance against Liverpool in their first game under Jaissle last Sunday, but suffered heartbreak as last-gasp penalty earned the Reds a 2-2 draw.

Newcastle introduced new signing Nico Gonzalez on the pitch before kick-off, and the need to have the Spaniard in their midfield was illustrated in the first half as early Championship pace-setters West Brom enjoyed surprising amounts of control against a Magpies side featuring six changes.

The Baggies were rewarded as Isaac Price caught out goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen with a fine free-kick to give them the lead.

Newcastle finished the second half strongly, though, and winger Bazoumana Toure marked his debut with a goal as he turned home from Amar Dedic’s right-wing cross.

The turnaround was completed by the 2025 winners three minutes into the second half when substitute Harvey Barnes crashed home from close range after West Brom failed to clear their lines after blocking his shot from the edge of the area following a corner.

Yet West Brom received a lifeline as Lewis Hall, who conceded the penalty against Liverpool, gave away another for handling a right-wing cross.

Price made no mistake with the spot-kick, but they were level for just four minutes as Barnes netted what proved to be the winner, converting from a Dedic cross after good work from Anthony Elanga.

Newcastle have been drawn away at Millwall in the third round.

Barry scores hat-trick and Johnson gets off mark for Everton

Everton enjoyed a more routine win as they cruised to a 4-0 win at Preston North End thanks to a Thierno Barry hat-trick.

Barry opened the scoring after Vitalii Mykolenko squared for him to tap in following a fine Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall pass.

Dewsbury-Hall was to the fore again as Barry made it 2-0, the ball rebounding in off the Frenchman after Preston goalkeeper Lee Nicholls could only parry the midfielder’s cross into his path.

Barry had another simple finish for his third, Brennan Johnson teeing him up to slot home after a quick attack again involving Dewsbury-Hall.

The favour was returned as Everton made it 4-0 when Johnson tucked home his first Everton goal from a well-weighted Barry pass. Everton will host Wolves in the third round.

Elsewhere, Bradford City booked their place in the third round, the League One side stunning Championship Burnley by beating them on penalties following a 0-0 draw at Valley Parade. Bradford’s reward is a tie with League One rivals Leyton Orient.

articles.title: Newcastle complete £52m signing of ‘proven winner’ Gonzalez
articles.summary: Gonzalez will likely make his debut against Spurs on Saturday.
articles.content:
Newcastle complete £52m signing of ‘proven winner’ Gonzalez

Gonzalez will likely make his debut against Spurs on Saturday.

Last Update:

Newcastle United have completed the signing of midfielder Nico Gonzalez from Manchester City.

The Magpies have made Gonzalez their seventh summer signing, paying an initial £48million to City, with the deal featuring a further £4m in potential add-ons.

After completing a medical on Tyneside on Wednesday, the signing of Gonzalez was announced ahead of their EFL Cup tie with Championship side West Brom.

Gonzalez will be expected to go straight into the team for Newcastle’s Premier League clash with Tottenham in North London on Saturday.

“I’m really happy to be here at this amazing club,” Gonzalez told Newcastle’s official website. “I’ve only heard top words about the club and the city, so I’m really excited to live here and to be part of this project.

“I love the black and white shirt already and I can’t wait to start wearing it on the pitch for this club.

“I’ve experienced playing at St. James’ Park twice with Manchester City and it was really tough. The atmosphere was amazing and the fans are so passionate. I can’t wait to experience that as a home player.”

Head coach Matthias Jaissle said: “I’m very happy to see Nico become a Newcastle United player. He brings serious quality and elite experience in a key area of the pitch.

“Nico is a really strong ball carrier – somebody who can drive the team forward while staying composed under pressure. He also brings discipline defensively, he reads the game well and his physicality makes him well suited to the Premier League.

“Nico is a proven winner who has already played at some huge clubs in Europe’s top leagues, but he’s also still young and hungry to develop further. He is a fantastic addition to our squad.”

The 24-year-old made 59 appearances in all competitions for City after joining from Porto in 2025. He scored four goals, including a stunning winner in the FA Cup semi-final against Southampton last season.

Now he will become the leader of a Newcastle midfield that has undergone significant changes this summer.

Gonzalez set for crucial role in Newcastle midfield

The arrival of the former Barcelona midfielder is the most significant of the transfer window for Newcastle, his signing helping fill the void left by former captain Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali, who left for Arsenal and Tottenham respectively.

He is the third midfielder to join Newcastle this summer, joining 18-year-old Sean Steur and 20-year-old Aladji Bamba.

Academy product Lewis Miley is a rising star who excelled in their thrilling season-opening 2-2 draw with Liverpool last Sunday, and he is the most likely midfield partner for Gonzalez against Spurs.

While Newcastle have plenty of young talent in their engine room, Gonzalez gives Newcastle a vastly more experienced defensive midfielder who can slot in immediately as their number six in new boss Jaissle’s system.

Gonzalez’s aptitude in possession should make him a huge asset to Newcastle. Since the Spaniard made his Premier League debut for City in February last year, only former team-mate Rodri (87) has made more successful passes per 90 minutes in the division than Gonzalez (68), according to Opta.

Newcastle are still hopeful of adding further to their ranks before the September 1 transfer deadline. Their next signing is likely to be an attacker, with Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo and Stuttgart’s Bilal El Khannouss thought to be among their targets.

articles.title: ‘For the moment, he is with us’ – Palace boss speaks out on Sarr to Liverpool speculation
articles.summary: Two of Palace's talismen have been linked with moves away.
articles.content:
‘For the moment, he is with us’ – Palace boss speaks out on Sarr to Liverpool speculation

Two of Palace's talismen have been linked with moves away.

Last Update:

Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage does not think it will be easy for Ismaila Sarr to leave the club amid interest from Liverpool, and also expects striker Jean-Philippe Mateta to remain at Selhurst Park.

Palace have reportedly rejected a £50million offer from Liverpool for Senegal winger Sarr, who missed their 2-0 defeat to Everton in their Premier League opener and is dealing with a groin injury.

Sarr is under contract until 2029, and Sage believes that status makes a potential move to Anfield unlikely.

Asked if he expects Sarr to stay at Palace, Sage told a press conference: “For the moment, yes.

“When you have three years on your contract, it’s not easy to leave. I understand for everyone if you have this kind of contact it’s difficult because you hesitate a lot but for the moment he is with us, he is under contract.

“He is injured and maybe you can make a link between injury and the situation but for me he is honest.

“I spoke with him this morning and yesterday about that with him but we just want him on the pitch and all the rest is for other people.”

Palace boss expects Mateta stay

Mateta has also been linked with a move away from south London, with Aston Villa reported to have made an offer for the France international’s services.

Palace and Mateta were involved in a dispute over the validity of one-year contract extension triggered by the club last season.

After the case was heard by a Premier League tribunal, Mateta and his representatives took the case to FIFA, only for world football’s governing body to deem it was not within their jurisdiction.

But Sage does not see a player who is desperate to leave and expects a positive outcome for Palace.

“I speak with him every day and in front of me I have a guy who is funny and happy to be here. He gives his best in every session,” Sage said ahead of Friday’s clash with Manchester City.

“I don’t see a player who has a problem with the club or with us. That’s why he played the last game as a starter.

“Imagine if you have a problem with us, he would not play as a starter. I think he will stay.

“Like, I told you he has the behaviour of someone who is happy to be here and wants to be here, and prepares to be here all season. I have no doubt about that.”

articles.title: ‘We expect Enzo to be involved’ – Fernandez set to play in Chelsea cup tie amid continued Man City interest
articles.summary: Enzo Fernandez is set to play for Chelsea in the EFL Cup on Thursday, but his future remains very much in doubt.
articles.content:
‘We expect Enzo to be involved’ – Fernandez set to play in Chelsea cup tie amid continued Man City interest

Enzo Fernandez is set to play for Chelsea in the EFL Cup on Thursday, but his future remains very much in doubt.

Last Update:

Xabi Alonso expects Enzo Fernandez to be involved in Chelsea‘s EFL Cup tie with Luton Town, but was noncommittal when asked about his future amid continued interest from Manchester City.

Former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca is keen to lure Fernandez to the Etihad Stadium as the final piece of City’s midfield revamp.

Chelsea had set a deadline of last Friday for City to sign the Argentina international. However, they are still said to be open to a sale if they get at least £120million and are able to sign a replacement.

Fernandez’s Chelsea future remains a doubt as transfer deadline nears

Fernandez was a second-half substitute as Alonso’s men began their Premier League campaign with a 3-2 win over west London rivals Fulham.

And, while Alonso is planning on having Fernandez available on Thursday against League One Luton, he did not give a commitment about him still being a Chelsea player after the September 1 transfer deadline.

“We expect Enzo to be involved. He’s training really well and he will be involved,” Alonso told a pre-match press conference.

Asked if he would Fernandez to remain with Chelsea beyond the deadline, Alonso replied: “We want to have the best team possible.

“We know his qualities, he has shown it and we have to wait, but we will think about tomorrow and let’s see how things develop.”

Chelsea have already made 11 signings in the transfer window, but Fernandez would leave a substantial hole if he did depart for City.

On the need for a replacement if a significant player leaves, Alonso said: “We assess the whole squad as a unit and in that squad we want good balance in terms of quality, in terms of positions, in terms of personalities, so we are aware of everything and we are prepared for whatever.”

articles.title: ‘There’s 0% chance of selling him to Barca’ – Atletico hit back after Laporta’s Alvarez comments
articles.summary: Atletico took a dim view of remarks from the Barca president.
articles.content:
‘There’s 0% chance of selling him to Barca’ – Atletico hit back after Laporta’s Alvarez comments

Atletico took a dim view of remarks from the Barca president.

Last Update:

Atletico Madrid have hit back at comments from Barcelona president Joan Laporta over the transfer saga surrounding Julian Alvarez, insisting there is a “0% chance” of him being sold to their LaLiga rivals.

Alvarez, who is under contract at the Metropolitano until 2030, stated his desire to fulfil his “dream” by moving to Barcelona during the World Cup.

The Argentina forward was booed and walked straight down the tunnel at full-time of Atletico’s LaLiga opener, a 2-2 draw with Villarreal, having come on as a second-half substitute.

Alvarez missed training on Wednesday, with the former Manchester City attacker reported as suffering from illness.

Atletico respond after Laporta interview

Arsenal still retain an interest in Alvarez, and the involvement of the Premier League champions is seemingly influencing Barca in keeping the public pressure on Atletico.

“Before anything, we have the utmost respect for Atletico de Madrid and a personal appreciation for their executives as well, because we’ve known each other for many years,” Laporta said in an interview posted to Barcelona’s social media channels on Wednesday.

“This whole situation has created a lot of noise. This is not motivated by actions taken by Barca. It is motivated by the fact that Atletico told us they were not selling [Alvarez]. However, it looks like, from what we hear now [Atletico reportedly being open to selling to Arsenal], they are trying to reach agreements with other clubs.

“I want to tell [CEO] Enrique Cerezo, with all the respect because I appreciate him a lot, that Barca have been up to the standards required in this situation, in the same way we do with other clubs.

“It happened to us in this window with Manchester City, as well as other clubs. We approach them to see if they want to sell one of their players. When they tell us they don’t sell, we let it go. But in this case, there are special circumstances that have been made aware Atletico de Madrid want to sell the player to other clubs.

“With this context, our interest and offer for the player remains up until the end of the window, in case Atletico de Madrid want to sell the player. We are very interested in buying Julian Alvarez. We would like our offer to be accepted. We say it with all the respect towards Atletico de Madrid.

“We want them to know that if they ever are open to selling the player before the end of the summer transfer window, we would be willing to buy him.”

Atletico responded in a statement reported by Marca: “The player is being portrayed as the victim, but the only victim of the Julian case is us.

“They have harmed us economically and socially. There is 0% chance of selling him to Barca. This situation is not about money, it’s about dignity.

“Theres a campaign with many lies and half-truths. The only one who pays for this is Atletico.”

articles.title: UEFA set to drop FIFA tournament boycott threat
articles.summary: UEFA are set to drop their threat of withdrawing from FIFA tournaments.
articles.content:
UEFA set to drop FIFA tournament boycott threat

UEFA are set to drop their threat of withdrawing from FIFA tournaments.

Last Update:

UEFA is expected to drop its threat to boycott FIFA competitions after receiving assurances that Gianni Infantino’s controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors will not be revived.

The issue will be discussed at a meeting of UEFA’s executive committee in Monaco on Thursday, with the governing body expected to formally lift the boycott threat.

UEFA had previously warned that the conditions needed to avoid a boycott had not been met, despite Fifa abandoning the proposal following widespread opposition.

The organisation had demanded guarantees that similar attempts to bring private ownership into Fifa competitions would not happen again.

Infantino later told national associations that the Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal was “now off the table” and apologised for the “errors” made during the process.

If UEFA removes its boycott threat, next month’s Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland will go ahead as planned.

Six European nations are due to compete in the tournament, with England, France, Italy, Portugal, Spain and hosts Poland all involved.

However, UEFA is not expected to soften its wider opposition to Infantino.

Infantino still not backed

European football’s governing body has led the backlash against the Fifa president and is expected to continue pushing for changes to the organisation’s leadership.

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has already said he expects Infantino either to resign or face a challenger when FIFA presidential election takes place in March.

Last month, all 55 of UEFA’s member associations voted to boycott FIFA competitions until the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal was completely abandoned and binding guarantees were provided that FIFA would not allow private ownership of its governance or competitions in future.

The proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise would have taken control of the commercial and ticketing rights for FIFA competitions, with a 21% stake initially earmarked for sale to a private investment company.

The dispute has led several national associations to withdraw their support for Infantino, who has been accused by UEFA, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation of breaking trust “through deception”.

articles.title: Chelsea considering move for Aston Villa keeper Martinez
articles.summary: Chelsea are exploring a possible move for Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez
articles.content:
Chelsea considering move for Aston Villa keeper Martinez

Chelsea are exploring a possible move for Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez

Last Update:

Chelsea are considering a move for Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez after making contact with the Argentina international’s representatives.

The 33-year-old could be available for a transfer after Villa signed Japan international Zion Suzuki from Parma for around £30m earlier this month.

Martinez has been Villa’s first-choice goalkeeper since joining from Arsenal in 2020, but his future at the club is now uncertain following Suzuki’s arrival.

Chelsea’s interest could lead to another deal between the two clubs after a busy summer of business.

The Blues signed Morgan Rogers from Villa for a club-record £117m, while Alejandro Garnacho moved in the opposite direction on an initial loan.

Nicolas Jackson is another player who could move between the clubs, with the Chelsea striker valued at around £65m and potentially set to reunite with former manager Unai Emery at Villa.

Martinez still searching for Villa exit

Martinez was also the subject of interest from Juventus earlier this summer, but that move collapsed after concerns over a finger injury.

Juventus instead signed Tottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario on loan.

Chelsea’s interest in Martinez comes amid questions over Robert Sanchez’s position as their first-choice goalkeeper.

Sanchez endured a difficult opening Premier League game against Fulham, conceding at his near post to Josh King before later spilling another effort that allowed Gonzalo Garcia to score.

Chelsea eventually won 3-2 at Craven Cottage, but the performance has increased scrutiny on Sanchez.

articles.title: Ayyoub Bouaddi: Man City sign Lille midfielder in £85.6m transfer
articles.summary: Ayyoub Bouaddi has completed his transfer from Lille to Man City
articles.content:
Ayyoub Bouaddi: Man City sign Lille midfielder in £85.6m transfer

Ayyoub Bouaddi has completed his transfer from Lille to Man City

Last Update:

Manchester City have signed Morocco international Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for £85.6m on a five-year deal.

Bouaddi, 18, has become the Premier League club’s fifth signing of the summer transfer window days after fellow midfielder Rodri’s move to Barcelona following seven years with City.

Speaking for the first time at his new club, the World Cup star said: “I wouldn’t be here without my family, so I am really happy to have them next to me.

“This is also why I am playing football, to make my family proud.

“I think the most important thing is to have balance and my family and parents are not always [about] football.

“It’s all the values that they teach me and it’s important to keep that.

“We need to be the same person with everybody, respect everyone, be myself, be yourself and just try to enjoy life.”

Table of Contents

Ayyoub Bouaddi: Why City made transfer move

Bouaddi has long been one of the best young players in France and announced himself on the European stage by playing throughout their home win over Real Madrid in October 2024 on his Champions League debut.

With Bernardo Silva and Rodri – two of the key midfielders in City’s period of dominating the Premier League under former manager Pep Guardiola – now gone, new City head coach Enzo Maresca is rebuilding his midfield.

The Italian is overseeing a squad in transition as he attempts to prove himself a worthy successor to Guardiola, who became the club’s most successful manager of all time during the Spaniard’s 10 years in charge until his exit in May.

A ball winner at the base of midfield, Bouaddi has the potential to replace some of the abilities that made Rodri a four-time Premier League champion and Champions League winner with the club, as well as the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner and player of the tournament at the World Cup 2026.

Maresca may be planning to pair Bouaddi with 23-year-old Elliot Anderson, who arrived from Nottingham Forest for £116m in July.

The former Chelsea manager is likely to have been among numerous admirers of Bouaddi’s performances at the World Cup, starting five of Morocco’s six matches and producing an exceptional display in their opening 1-1 draw with Brazil.

Ayyoub Bouaddi style of play

Lille veteran and former Arsenal and Chelsea striker Olivier Giroud calls Bouaddi “somewhat reminiscent” of legendary midfielder N’Golo Kante.

“He’s calm, confident and remains himself,” Giroud told BBC Sport. “I was talking to some friends and they sent me some photos of Patrick Vieira and Sergio Busquets. They said he’s a mix of both.

“Technically he’s not quite at the level of Sergio Busquets yet, but he’s got the skills. He might lack the power of Patrick.

“He’ll get stronger and bigger with time but he’s already a very versatile player. He can do everything.

“The only thing he needs to work on – and he knows this because we’ve teased him a lot this year – is finishing. He needs to be more aggressive in front of goal.”

Ayyoub Bouaddi 🌟 👶 Just 18 years old… #UCL pic.twitter.com/JYYlcmKw7X

Ayyoub Bouaddi: Arsenal miss out on transfer

Reigning Premier League champions Arsenal were one of the clubs linked with Bouaddi, although their 3-0 win over City in the Community Shield on August 16 – and Anderson and Mateo Kovacic’s unconvincing performances as part of a poor City display – suggested they were less in need of players in his position.

Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City and Bayern Munich were also interested in Bouaddi, Metro reported on June 30.

Citing RMC Sport, the outlet said Lille wanted to sell for up to £89m but were willing to accept a lower fee if he was loaned back to them this season.

Ayyoub Bouaddi stats: Lille, Morocco

Lille’s trust in Bouaddi has allowed him to break several age records, including the feat of becoming the youngest player ever in a European club competition game by featuring in the Conference League three days after his 16th birthday in October 2023.

Seventeen days later, Bouaddi made his first appearance in Ligue 1 to become the youngest appearance-maker in the French top flight for 42 years.

Bouaddi signed a contract extension until 2029 in December 2025. The following month, he broke former Premier League Player of the Season Eden Hazard’s record as the youngest player to make 50 Ligue 1 appearances for Lille.

Morocco considered Bouaddi’s switch of allegiance in May 2026 a major coup following his appearances at youth level for France, with their pursuit rewarded by his World Cup performances.

Here are some of Bouaddi’s key stats in Ligue 1 2025/26.

articles.title: When is the Champions League draw? Date, time, schedule, where to watch
articles.summary: The competition is in its 72nd season
articles.content:
When is the Champions League draw? Date, time, schedule, where to watch

The competition is in its 72nd season

Last Update:

The Champions League draw for the 2026/27 edition of the competition will schedule the initial eight matches for each of the teams taking part.

Reigning French champions Paris Saint-Germain will defend the title they retained by beating Arsenal on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the 2025/26 final.

Premier League holders the Gunners and runners-up Manchester City will be joined by Manchester United, Aston Villa and Liverpool in the draw.

Here’s what you need to know about the Champions League draw, including when it takes place, when future draws are and the fixture schedule for 2026/27.

Table of Contents

When is the Champions League league phase draw?

The draw will take place on Thursday, August 27 – a day after the play-off ties come to a close to decide the last teams to qualify.

The draw ceremony will start at 17:00 BST / 12:00 ET / 09:00 PT.

How to watch the Champions League draw: TV channel, live stream

The draw will be shown live and for free on UEFA.com, as well as on UEFA’s YouTube channel.

TNT Sports will also broadcast the draw on TNT Sports 1 and the HBO Max app.

Champions League format

In a change from the group stage format conducted until 2023/24, each team now plays eight matches in the league phase, all against different opponents.

Four of those matches will be at home and four away, with the opponents determined according to four seeding pots split by rankings.

Teams will play two opponents from each of those pots – one against a team from each pot at home and one away. The results decide the overall standings in one league.

The top eight sides in the table qualify automatically for the round of 16. The teams finishing in ninth to 24th will compete in a two-legged knockout phase play-off to reach the last 16.

Teams finishing 25th or lower are out of Europe for the season.

Champions League schedule, fixtures 2026/27

The league phase starts on September 8 and runs until the end of January.

When is the Champions League knockout phase?

The knockout stage starts with the play-offs to reach the round of 16 in February.

When are the Champions League draws?

The dates for the knockout stage draws were yet to be confirmed as of August 25, 2026.

English teams in the Champions League: Why are there five clubs?

Arsenal, City, United, Villa and Liverpool.qualified as the top five teams in the Premier League.

England was awarded extra positions as a result of UEFA’s co-efficient rankings, which are based on the overall performances of nations across European competition over a season.

Villa also won last season’s Europa League, which would have earned the Villans a place in the Champions League had they not qualified through their league position.

When is the Champions League final?

The final will take place on June 5 2027 at the Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid, which has been Atletico Madrid’s home since 2017.

That could be a good omen for English teams: two Premier League sides reached the final when Atleti’s home previously hosted the showpiece in 2019, Liverpool beating Tottenham 2-0.

articles.title: Marmoush set to undergo Tottenham medical ahead of £50m move from Manchester City
articles.summary: Omar Marmoush is set to join Tottenham and undergo his medical on Wednesday.
articles.content:
Marmoush set to undergo Tottenham medical ahead of £50m move from Manchester City

Omar Marmoush is set to join Tottenham and undergo his medical on Wednesday.

Last Update:

Omar Marmoush is set to undergo a medical at Tottenham after Manchester City agreed a loan deal for the forward that includes an obligation for Spurs to buy him permanently.

The deal will guarantee City £50m, with a further £10m available in add-ons, including £5m guaranteed.

Marmoush is expected to sign a four-year contract with Tottenham, with the option of a further season. No sell-on fee will be owed to his former club Eintracht Frankfurt.

The Egypt international’s move comes just days after Tottenham completed an £85m deal for his Manchester City team-mate Savio.

Spurs had been working on both deals this week as Roberto De Zerbi continues to reshape his squad ahead of the new season.

Marmoush’s departure from City is a relatively quick turnaround for a player who only joined the club in January 2025.

City paid around £59m to £63m to sign him from Frankfurt after an impressive start to the 2024-25 season in Germany, where he scored 20 goals in 26 appearances.

He made an immediate impact at the Etihad, scoring seven goals in 16 appearances during the second half of that campaign.

However, his opportunities became more limited last season.

Marmoush scored eight goals in 36 appearances across all competitions, but only eight of those appearances were starts in the Premier League. He came off the bench 13 times in the competition.

He was also included in City’s squad for the Community Shield against Arsenal on 16 August, replacing Erling Haaland in the second half of their 3-0 defeat.

The move to Tottenham would give Marmoush the opportunity to play a more prominent role under De Zerbi, while City would receive a significant fee for a player who had fallen down the pecking order.

Tottenham have already spent heavily this summer as they look to strengthen their squad.

Their permanent additions include Savio, Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Jan Paul van Hecke, with the club spending more than £300m on those four players.

Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi and Martin Dubravka have also arrived as free agents.

articles.title: O’Neill takes blame for Celtic’s humiliating Champions League exit
articles.summary: Martin O'Neill has taken the blame for Celtic blowing a four goal lead in the Champions League.
articles.content:
O’Neill takes blame for Celtic’s humiliating Champions League exit

Martin O'Neill has taken the blame for Celtic blowing a four goal lead in the Champions League.

Last Update:

Martin O’Neill has accepted full responsibility after Celtic suffered a remarkable Champions League collapse against LASK, throwing away a four-goal aggregate lead to crash out of qualifying.

Celtic appeared to have the tie under control after winning the first leg, but their advantage disappeared during a chaotic second half in Austria.

LASK eventually forced extra time before completing a stunning 5-4 aggregate comeback, leaving Celtic to reflect on one of the most painful European exits in recent years.

O’Neill made no attempt to shift the blame after the final whistle.

“I’m responsible for this one,” he said. “Without a doubt.”

In the context of things, one was a final which it would have been terrific to win, this was a qualifying game which we should have been able to get through,” O’Neill added.

“We know that we are a million miles from the finished article. That’s absolutely true. I think we thought that anyway.”

The result is particularly damaging given Celtic’s experience of European disappointment at the same stage last year.

O’Neill was not in charge when Brendan Rodgers’ side were eliminated by Kairat Almaty on penalties, but that defeat contributed to the eventual end of Rodgers’ second spell at the club.

O’Neill subsequently took over and helped restore some stability, guiding Celtic to another Scottish Premiership title and the Scottish Cup after a turbulent period.

The collapse in Austria now leaves him with another major rebuilding job.

UCL failure brings consequences

Celtic will have to regroup quickly, but their failure to reach the Champions League also has serious financial consequences.

Qualification would have brought a significant boost to the club’s finances and made Celtic a more attractive destination for potential new signings during the final stages of the transfer window.

O’Neill acknowledged that the club’s recruitment plans could now be affected.

“The qualification for the Champions League is major, it’s major in every aspect,” he said. “Financially, for prestige, but we have to pick ourselves up. That’s my responsibility again to do that.

“I think I said last week that if you could qualify for the Champions League there would be players wanting to come on that basis,” he said.

“That’s not going to be the case but we’ll see.”

articles.content:
Carabao Cup: Leeds, Ipswich, Coventry, Hull and Brentford through

Forest only Premier League side to be knocked out

Last Update:

Brentford hit six while Leeds knocked out Nottingham Forest in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

Leeds beat Forest for the second time in just a few days thanks to second-half goals from Daniel James and James Justin.

The hosts made the brighter start with James Trafford forced into a sharp early stop from Ola Aina before Justin cleared Igor Jesus’ goal-bound header. However, Leeds gradually asserted control in an open first half, threatening through Sean Longstaff and James while Joe Rodon produced a crucial last-ditch challenge at the other end to deny Chris Wood.

The breakthrough arrived five minutes after the restart when Longstaff seized on Aina’s misplaced header, driving forward to slip in James, who maintained his composure to clip neatly past Matz Sels. Forest pushed hard for an instant equaliser, but Trafford was again equal to Wood’s low effort, allowing Leeds to keep their noses in front amidst heavy home pressure.

Farke’s men sealed the tie with 15 minutes remaining via a scrappy goalmouth scramble, as Justin ultimately forced the ball home over the line after Lucas Nmecha’s initial effort was blocked.

Ipswich continued their winning start by beating Leicester 3-1, with goals from Sindre Egeli and a double for Marcelino Nunez, while Callum Wilson scored his first for Brentford in a thumping 6-1 win at Birmingham.

Hull needed penalties to win at Stoke, and Victor Torp fired home a penalty as Coventry City rallied late to hold off Plymouth Argyle.
